title: Vice-President calls for holistic rural development to realise Viksit Bharat 2047; graces Golden Jubilee Celebrations and 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute
subtitle:
“India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047 must begin with empowered villages”: Vice-President

Gandhian ideals of self-reliance and social service remain vital for building a developed India: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 3:02PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today graced the Golden Jubilee Celebrations and 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute (Deemed to be University) in Dindigul, Tamil Nadu. He conferred gold medals on meritorious students and extended his congratulations and best wishes to all the graduating students.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the Golden Jubilee Celebrations and 39th Convocation of Gandhigram Rural Institute (Deemed to be University), Dindigul, Tamil Nadu, today, and conferred gold medals on meritorious students.

Emphasising that Viksit Bharat 2047 begins with developed villages, he highlighted the transformative progress in rural infrastructure and basic amenities over the past twelve years and called for ensuring greater opportunities and a dignified life for every rural citizen.

Governor of Tamil Nadu Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, Chancellor Dr. K. M. Annamalai, Vice-Chancellor Dr. N. Panchanatham and other dignitaries were present.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 30, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President emphasised that the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 can be realised only through the holistic development of villages. He stated that the real strength of Indialies in its villages and that rural development must remain a fundamental pillar of national development.
He stressed that the objective should not necessarily be to transform every village into a town, but to ensure that rural citizens have access to quality infrastructure, essential public services, livelihood opportunities and a dignified standard of living comparable to those available in urban areas.
Recalling the legacy of Mahatma Gandhi, the Vice-President said that the history of Gandhigram was closely intertwined with Gandhian philosophy. He recalled that Dr. G. Ramachandran and Dr. T. S. Soundaram Ramachandran, inspired by Mahatma Gandhi’s ideals, established the institution with the vision of promoting rural education, development and social transformation.
Highlighting the enduring power of truth and non-violence, he observed that Mahatma Gandhi had challenged the might of the British Empire through these principles and led India to freedom. Gandhian values, he said, continue to offer guidance to society and the nation.
Referring to India’s development journey over the past twelve years under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President highlighted significant progress in rural housing, drinking water, electricity, roads, sanitation, agriculture and digital connectivity.
He noted that, approximately 25 crore people moved out of multidimensional poverty between 2014 and 2023. He observed that various development and welfare initiatives had contributed to improving the quality of life of millions of people.
Emphasising the importance of connectivity, he said that villages must be linked to towns and cities through improved road and transport infrastructure so that opportunities in education, healthcare, markets and employment reach rural communities.
He also underlined the impact of the Swachh Bharat Mission in creating greater awareness about cleanliness. Referring to improvements in the cleanliness of public spaces, he stressed that cleanliness was not merely the responsibility of the government but a collective responsibility of every citizen.
Stating that farmers’ welfare was directly linked to the country’s food security, he highlighted the importance of supporting the farming community. He referred to the PM-KISAN scheme, under which eligible farmer families receive financial assistance of ₹6,000 annually in three instalments directly into their bank accounts.
The Vice-President observed that Artificial Intelligence, automation and digital technologies were rapidly transforming the world and changing the nature of employment. He urged students to equip themselves with emerging technologies while developing creativity, problem-solving abilities and an entrepreneurial outlook.
He encouraged them to become job creators rather than merely job seekers. Referring to the contemporary relevance of Mahatma Gandhi’s philosophy of Swadeshi, he said that promoting domestic manufacturing, indigenous technologies, local industries and innovations by young Indians represented the modern expression of Swadeshi.
The Vice-President called upon the graduating students to use their education and skills not merely for personal advancement but also for the welfare of society. He urged them to make Gandhian values of simplicity, self-reliance, social responsibility and service the guiding principles of their lives.
He also urged students to stay away from drugs and substance abuse and become ambassadors of a drug-free society by creating awareness among their friends, families and communities.
Congratulating Gandhigram Rural Institute on completing fifty years of its journey as a deemed-to-be university, the Vice-President expressed confidence that it would continue to emerge as a leading centre for sustainable rural development, inclusive growth and innovative research.
On the occasion, the Vice-President conferred Honorary Doctorates (Honoris Causa) on three distinguished personalities in recognition of their outstanding contributions in their respective fields: Thavathiru Kundrakudi Ponnambala Adigalar, renowned spiritual leader and Tamil scholar; Shri S. Nambi Narayanan, former senior aerospace scientist of ISRO; and Professor S. S. M. Sundaram, distinguished academician.

title: BOOKS ARE POWERFUL INSTRUMENTS OF TRANSFORMING LIVES AND BRINGING POSITIVE CHANGE IN SOCIETY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
subtitle:
TECHNOLOGY CAN PROVIDE INFORMATION, BUT TRUE KNOWLEDGE COMES FROM BOOKS AND LIFE EXPERIENCES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

INDIA'S DEMOCRACY IS ITS GREATEST STRENGTH, UNITING THE NATION AMID EXTRAORDINARY DIVERSITY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LANGUAGES DO NOT DIVIDE US; THEY CONNECT PEOPLE AND STRENGTHEN OUR CULTURAL BONDS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESS INAUGURAL CEREMONY OF THE 29TH KOCHI INTERNATIONAL BOOK FESTIVAL IN KERALAM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 9:37PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today emphasised that books are not merely sources of information but powerful instruments of transforming lives, broadening perspectives and inspiring positive change in society. He observed that while technology has made information readily accessible, true knowledge and wisdom come from books and life experiences. Stressing that there is no substitute for books, he said that reading not only enriches individuals but also cultivates curiosity, sensitivity and the ability to understand life from different perspectives.
Addressing the inaugural ceremony of the 29th Kochi International Book Festival in Kochi, Shri Birla emphasised the importance of cultivating reading habits and inspiring others to read. He observed that books preserve generations of wisdom and experience, inspire and guide individuals and foster discipline, determination and a sense of purpose.
Drawing a distinction between information and knowledge, Shri Birla observed that digital technology has enhanced access to information, but books and human experiences remain vital for deeper understanding and sensitivity. Emphasising lifelong learning, he highlighted curiosity as essential to acquiring knowledge and noted that books inspire hope, resilience and the pursuit of constructive goals.
Highlighting India's extraordinary diversity, Shri Birla said that the country's varied languages, religions, traditions, perspectives and ways of life constitute its unique strength. He observed that despite these differences, India remains united, and democracy is the greatest force binding the nation together. Shri Birla emphasised that democracy teaches people to respect differing opinions and ideologies and to live together in harmony. He further stressed that while opinions may differ, all citizens must stand united when it comes to the interests of the nation.
Speaking on the role of language and literature in promoting national unity, Shri Birla observed that languages connect rather than divide people. He highlighted the contribution of India's rich linguistic traditions, including Malayalam, Kannada and Telugu, in preserving and promoting the country's cultural, spiritual and intellectual heritage. He noted that writers have taken India's history, values and democratic ideals to the world, while digital translation has further expanded literature's reach across linguistic boundaries.
Appreciating Keralam's contributions to education, literature, science and technology, Shri Birla highlighted its distinction as India's first fully literate State. He observed that education has enabled Keralites to excel in India and abroad, while praising the State's traditions of service and sacrifice, particularly the contribution of its women to nursing and healthcare worldwide. Recalling Shri P. N. Panicker's pioneering contribution to Keralam's library movement, he observed that libraries and reading habits had transformed literacy and socio-economic development. He highlighted the Kerala Granthasala movement's role in spreading knowledge and appreciated Keralam's sustained efforts to promote reading through 'Vayana Dinam' or Reading Day, observed on 19 June.
Shri Birla commended the organisers of the Kochi International Book Festival for bringing together literary stakeholders and promoting literature. He observed that such festivals encourage intellectual exchange, nurture reading habits and provide access to diverse ideas. He called for greater efforts to take Kerala's rich literary, spiritual and cultural heritage to India and the world through books and translations. He congratulated the organisers and expressed hope that the Kochi International Book Festival would continue to expand its reach, inspire new generations of readers and contribute to building a more knowledgeable, sensitive and enlightened society.
Former ISRO Chairman Dr. S. Somanath, Chairman of the International Book Festival Shri Madhu S. Nair, Shri Prakash Babu, Sahitya Akademi Secretary Dr. Varun Gulati, several distinguished guests, literary figures and book enthusiasts were present on the occasion.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi  lays the foundation stone, inaugurates and dedicates to the Nation development projects worth over ₹14,000 Crore in Banaskantha, Gujarat
subtitle:
From farms and dairy to infrastructure and connectivity, Banaskantha is making new strides in development: PM

Our farmers, our Annadatas, are one of the strongest pillars of a Viksit Bharat, and our government has always prioritized the welfare of farmers and their empowerment: PM

Animal husbandry forms a vital pillar of our rural economy; Over the last decade, we have also heavily emphasized leveraging science and technology in this sector and dairy: PM

We are making animal husbandry not just a tradition, but a strong instrument to increase farmers' income and bring prosperity to our villages: PM

Until the final moment of my life, I will remain devoted only to your service: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 4:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone, inaugurated, and dedicated to the nation development projects worth over ₹14,000 crore today in Banaskantha, Gujarat. Speaking on the sacred soil of Mother Amba shortly after Navratri, he unveiled multiple initiatives for women, children, farmers, and cattle rearers, while also disbursing a fresh installment of the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi to tens of millions of small farmers nationwide.
Describing farmers and annadatas as among the strongest pillars of a Viksit Bharat, the Prime Minister stated that the government has consistently prioritized their welfare and empowerment, increasing the national agricultural budget more than fivefold compared to 2013-14. Noting that the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi has become an integral part of small farmers' lives, he highlighted that over 1,000 crore rupees have been deposited into the accounts of more than 50 lakh farmers in Gujarat, including nearly 50 crore rupees for lakhs of farming families in Banaskantha. “Today, an amount of more than 18 thousand crore rupees has been sent into the accounts of about 10 crore farmers,” noted PM Modi.
Highlighting that government policies over recent years have delivered or saved more than 50 lakh crore rupees for farmers, the Prime Minister cited the first of five key examples by pointing out that nearly 4.5 lakh crore rupees have been transferred directly into the bank accounts of small farmers under the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi. He observed that  small farmers constitute over 85 percent of the farming community and our  government cared for such small farmers and provided them help through PM Kisan Samman Nidhi,” asserted Shri Modi.
Pointing to the sharp surge in global fertilizer prices amid international uncertainty over the past few years, the Prime Minister emphasized that his farmer-centric government shielded cultivators from the price hike. “The government spent about 16 lakh crore rupees on this,” noted PM Modi.
The Prime Minister underscored that the government fulfilled its MSP commitment. “In the past 12 years, wheat and paddy farmers have received more than 24 lakh crore rupees as MSP,” observed Shri Modi.
Spotlighting the strong security shield provided to cultivators through the PM Fasal Bima Yojana, the Prime Minister stated that farmers have received over 2 lakh crore rupees in crop insurance compensation over the last 10 to 12 years, alongside continuous efforts to reduce irrigation costs through the expanding role of the PM-KUSUM scheme. He explained that the distribution of nearly 12 lakh solar pumps under the scheme has generated additional electricity and saved lakhs of farmers the expense of purchasing over 80 crore liters of diesel, bringing the total financial benefit or savings from just these five major schemes and decisions to 50 lakh crore rupees. “These 50 lakh crore rupees have increased the income of the country's farmers and enhanced the capability of agriculture in India,” asserted PM Modi.
Emphasizing that agriculture is both a tradition and a vital part of Indian culture, the Prime Minister stated that the government has extensively integrated science and technology into farming and animal husbandry over the past 12 years. He cited the Soil Health Card as a prime example that resolved farmers' earlier difficulties in determining the exact type and quantity of fertilizer required for their fields, modernizing agricultural practices across the country. “Today more than 26 crore Soil Health Cards are with the country's farmers,” noted Shri Modi.
Acknowledging that changing weather patterns pose a major challenge to cultivators, the Prime Minister stated that the government is continuously striving to provide farmers with new climate-resilient seed varieties. “In recent years, about three thousand new varieties of seeds have been made available to farmers,” observed PM Modi.
Highlighting animal husbandry as a vital component of the rural economy with massive participation from rural women, the Prime Minister emphasized the integration of science and technology into the dairy and livestock sector over the past decade. He explained that superior animal breeds boost milk yields while timely vaccination and medical treatment curb losses from disease. “Meaning, if the animal is healthy, the earnings of my livestock-rearing brothers and sisters will also increase,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Spotlighting the Rashtriya Gokul Mission's role in promoting the conservation and scientific breeding of indigenous livestock, the Prime Minister noted that the newly built research center in Banaskantha will strengthen this mission by conserving and improving the quality of indigenous cow breeds like Gir, Sahiwal, and Kankrej, as well as buffalo breeds like Mehsana, Murrah, and Jaffarabadi, serving as the country's first such facility for the Kankrej breed. He explained that when a farmer wishes to pass down the traits of a high-yielding, low-maintenance, healthy cow to future generations, modern technologies like IVF increase the probability of transferring those superior qualities. “The livestock farmer will get its direct benefit,” noted PM Modi.
Stating that protecting livestock from ailments like foot-and-mouth disease is a key priority because such illnesses impact both animal health and milk yields, the Prime Minister highlighted the launch of a nationwide free vaccination drive. He pointed out that about 150 crore vaccine doses have been administered so far, providing free vaccination to the livestock of over 8 crore farmers. “This has also reduced the financial burden on livestock farmers,” observed Shri Modi.
Pointing to the visible impact of these interventions on dairy output, the Prime Minister noted that average daily milk yield per cow or buffalo has risen from under 5 liters in 2013-14 to nearly 8 liters today, giving India the fastest milk productivity growth rate in the world and benefiting rural farming families. “India is number one in the world in milk production,” remarked PM Modi.
Expressing the government's resolve to help livestock rearers earn from cow dung as well as milk, the Prime Minister stated that infrastructure is being built with the vital support of institutions like Banas Dairy to produce biogas, bio-CNG, and organic fertilizer from dung and farm residue, marked by the foundation stone laying of two bio-CNG plants today. He underscored the clear objective of keeping livestock healthy, increasing milk yields, and ensuring the complete utilization of dung. “We are making animal husbandry not just a tradition, but a powerful instrument for increasing farmers' income and enriching villages,” asserted Shri Modi.
Explaining that the government has worked with a holistic approach over recent years to ensure rural prosperity, the Prime Minister pointed to the vast expansion of the fisheries sector and the promotion of cooperatives within it. “You will be glad to hear that India's seafood exports have more than doubled,” noted PM Modi.
Highlighting beekeeping as another major avenue of supplementary income for farmers, the Prime Minister noted that honey production has doubled over the past 12 years and lauded the growing contribution of women's Self-Help Groups in driving this Madhu Kranti. “You will be proud to know that our country has become the second-largest exporter of natural honey,” observed Shri Modi.
Recalling that on October 7 he completed 25 years of service as the head of a government after first taking oath on October 7, 2001, the Prime Minister reflected on the immense love and guidance he received from every Gujarati at a time when he knew nothing of government offices or official files. He expressed gratitude to the people for entrusting a person from a poor family, whose ancestors never even dreamed of becoming a village sarpanch, with the responsibility of serving first Gujarat and then the nation. “And even more than love, every single Gujarati has taught me and led me on the right path,” remarked PM Modi.
Stating that he only knew the two guiding principles of serving the nation through public service and developing the country through Gujarat's development while learning everything else from the people, the Prime Minister credited citizens for whatever he has achieved for the nation. “For this, I will remain indebted to you for life, and until the last moment of life, I will remain engaged in your service,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Reminding older citizens of the acute water and electricity shortages that plagued the region 25 years ago, the Prime Minister recalled how the people heeded his appeal to conserve both resources and transformed their circumstances so thoroughly that those old hardships now remain only in memories. “I will say the same thing to you again today, that we have to save water, save electricity,” urged PM Modi.
Highlighting how Narmada waters and modern technologies like drip irrigation have transformed Banaskantha and made its potatoes world-famous alongside Banas Dairy's expansion of the cooperative movement to Kashi and beyond, the Prime Minister pointed out that the capacity of the potato plant that makes French fries has also been increased to enable greater procurement of potatoes. “This is a very big facility for potato farmers,” noted Shri Modi.
Detailing the ongoing cluster development program for fruit and vegetable cultivators under which 12 clusters were approved today for tomato, potato, chili, grapes, banana, onion, orange, pomegranate, and cocoa, the Prime Minister stated that farmers are receiving subsidies to plant new orchards and rejuvenate old ones. “The two clusters received in North Gujarat will greatly benefit the potato farmers of Banaskantha and Sabarkantha,” observed PM Modi.
Listing several major infrastructure projects inaugurated or initiated for Gujarat's development today, the Prime Minister highlighted the flagging off of two new rail services, the Ahmedabad-Varanasi Sabarmati Express and the Mehsana-Becharaji-Sabarmati MEMU train, alongside the expansion of the Ahmedabad Metro with foundation stones laid for metro projects connecting GIFT City and the airport. “The Ahmedabad-Mehsana highway is now going to become eight-lane from four-lane,” noted Shri Modi.
Spotlighting new social welfare infrastructure launched for the children of the state today, the Prime Minister noted that over 4,000 modern Anganwadis have been inaugurated across Gujarat. “This will benefit about 4 lakh children and pregnant mothers,” observed PM Modi.
Stating that every such developmental effort is aimed at building a developed India as every farmer, youth, sister, and daughter marches forward with the resolve of a Viksit Bharat, the Prime Minister remarked that unfortunately some elements dislike this progress and wish to see the nation in difficulty. “When crises befall the country, they feel happy,” remarked Shri Modi.
Citing the ongoing war around Iran and the Gulf countries as a recent example where India stood united to face the situation while certain elements spread rumors to scare farmers about fertilizer shortages and women about gas supplies, the Prime Minister stated that their plan was to trigger chaos in the country to defame him. “When India was engaged in facing this unitedly, then these people kept spreading rumors,” remarked PM Modi.
Reminding the farming community of his solemn assurance to stand firmly beside them, the Prime Minister pointed out that the government prevented any scarcity of agricultural inputs despite the ongoing conflict.
Noting that the war caused global prices of fertilizers and raw chemicals to skyrocket, the Prime Minister highlighted that the government shielded Indian cultivators from the burden, providing a bag of urea that costs 3,000 rupees globally for under 300 rupees in India, and supplying a bag of DAP that exceeds 5,000 rupees internationally for just 1,350 rupees. “The country is providing this help so that our farmer is empowered, and the farmer's life becomes better,” affirmed PM Modi.
Emphasizing that India's rapid development offers new hope to an uncertain world and requires marching continuously on the path of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat, the Prime Minister noted that October 31 marks National Unity Day when the entire nation runs with the inspiration of unity amid grand preparations for the Run for Unity. “I would urge all countrymen, especially my young companions, to participate enthusiastically in the Run for Unity tomorrow morning,” exhorted Shri Modi.
Pointing out a schedule change for the annual Unity Festival at Ekta Nagar on October 31, the Prime Minister announced that this year's celebrations will take place grandly at 5:30 PM tomorrow evening featuring police and security force parades and tableaus, and urged citizens from Kashmir to Kanyakumari and Kutch to Kamakhya to join the event and bow to Sardar Patel while reiterating the resolve of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat. “With this request, once again best wishes to all of you for the development works,” concluded PM Modi.

content:
Bharat Mata Ki Jai.
Bharat Mata Ki Jai.
Popular Chief Minister of Gujarat Shri Bhupendra Bhai Patel, Deputy Chief Minister Bhai Harsh Sanghvi ji, Speaker of the Legislative Assembly Shri Shankarbhai Chaudhary, all ministers of the Gujarat Government, Members of Parliament and Members of the Legislative Assembly, other public representatives, brothers and sisters.
Today, through technology, farmers from every district of the country are connected with us. Today, through technology, farmers from every village of Gujarat are connected with us. Chief Ministers of different states, ministers, all of them are with us today in this important programme for farmers. I heartily welcome all of them as well.
Today, Banaskantha has established its stature. Just now, I was watching on the screen that perhaps such a large gathering seated on charpoys has never been held anywhere in the world. For the people of the country too, it must be an amazing sight that everyone in this gathering is seated on charpoys. Today, Banaskantha has revived this great tradition of our villages. Had you informed the Guinness Book of World Records in advance, they would certainly have recorded it as a world record. It was just mentioned here a moment ago.
The responsibility that you entrusted to me has now completed twenty-five years. And look at the coincidence, after completing twenty-five years, my first visit has been to our Banaskantha. Let me remind you that after becoming Chief Minister in 2001, my first major public programme as Chief Minister was held in Deesa. The older people here will remember that Lok Kalyan Mela. That programme was perhaps historic. Three lakh people from a single district attended it. I do not believe that record has been broken to this day. That record belongs to Banaskantha. The journey began there, and today I have got the opportunity to present an account of twenty-five years of service at the same place.
Only a few days after Navratri, I have received the opportunity to come to the sacred land of Mother Amba. I bow at the feet of Mother Amba. A short while ago, projects dedicated to women, children, farmers, and livestock rearers were inaugurated and foundation stones laid here. A new instalment of PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi has also reached the accounts of crores of small farmers across the country. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to the people of Gujarat, to the people of the country, and to farmers across India.
Friends,
The people of Gujarat and Banaskantha should forgive me, but I have to speak in Hindi today because people from all over the country are connected with this programme. You permit me to speak in Hindi, don't you? Very good.
Friends,
Our farmers, our food providers, are among the strongest pillars of a Developed India. Our government has always prioritised the welfare and empowerment of farmers. Compared to 2013–14, the agricultural budget of the country has now increased more than five times. PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi has become a part of the lives of crores of small farmers. Today, more than ₹18,000 crore has been transferred into the accounts of nearly ten crore farmers. More than fifty lakh farmers of Gujarat have also benefited from it. More than ₹1,000 crore has been deposited into their accounts. In Banaskantha alone, nearly ₹50 crore has reached the accounts of lakhs of farming families.
Friends,
Because of our government's policies over the past years, farmers have received benefits or savings worth more than ₹50 lakh crore. Fifty lakh crore rupees. Let me give you an example of just five schemes. Around ₹4.5 lakh crore under PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi has directly reached the bank accounts of small farmers. Sister, you have defeated me. I thought you would sit down after a while because your hands would start hurting. I request the SPG personnel to collect that beautiful picture which this daughter has brought. Otherwise, she will grow tired holding it up. They will collect it from here, my child. Please stay where you are. Let the SPG personnel collect it. After Independence, the needs of small farmers were never truly understood. Nobody paid attention to them. Yet small farmers account for more than 85 percent of all farmers in our country. More than 85 percent. It is our government that understood their concerns and supported them through PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi.
Friends,
Over the past few years, global uncertainties caused fertiliser prices to surge sharply. But a government dedicated to farmers did not allow that burden to fall upon them. The government spent nearly ₹16 lakh crore on this. To ensure that fertilisers remain affordable for you, we had to spend ₹16 lakh crore from the national treasury, so that the burden would not fall upon our farmers.
Friends,
Previous governments repeatedly misled farmers on Minimum Support Price. But ours is the government that fulfilled its MSP promise. Over the past twelve years, farmers growing wheat and paddy have received ₹24 lakh crore in MSP payments directly into their accounts.
Friends,
Our government has provided farmers with a powerful safety net through the PM Fasal Bima Yojana. We launched crop insurance on a large scale. During the past ten to twelve years, farmers have received more than ₹2 lakh crore in crop insurance compensation. Whenever crops suffered losses, over ₹2 lakh crore reached farmers through insurance support. We are continuously trying to reduce farmers' irrigation costs as well. PM-KUSUM is playing an increasingly significant role in this effort. Under this scheme, nearly twelve lakh solar pumps have already been provided. Twelve lakh pumps powered by solar energy have been given to farmers for irrigation. Because of this, the need for electricity and diesel has reduced substantially. If these solar pumps had not been provided, farmers would have had to purchase more than 80 crore litres of diesel. That entire expense has been saved by lakhs of farmers. And besides that, additional electricity has also been generated. If viewed in one way, these five schemes and decisions alone have either directly benefited farmers or saved them the equivalent of ₹50 lakh crore. This is an enormous figure. These ₹50 lakh crore have increased farmers’ incomes and strengthened Indian agriculture.
Friends,
Agriculture is our tradition. Agriculture is our culture. Agriculture is our culture. During the past twelve years, our government has extensively integrated science and technology into farming. We have linked agriculture and animal husbandry with scientific methods. Soil Health Cards are an excellent example of this. Earlier, farmers found it difficult to determine what type of fertilizer their fields required and in what quantity. Soil Health Cards solved this problem. Today, more than 26 crore Soil Health Cards are in the hands of farmers. These have modernised farming practices.
Friends,
Changing weather patterns are a major challenge for farmers. Therefore, our effort is to continuously provide farmers with new seed varieties that are better suited to changing climatic conditions. Over the past years, around three thousand new seed varieties have been made available to farmers.
Friends,
Animal husbandry is an important part of our rural economy, and our sisters have a major role in it. During the past decade, we have strongly promoted the use of science and technology in animal husbandry and the dairy sector. When livestock breeds improve, milk production increases. As Shankarbhai was saying earlier, we want one cow to produce as much milk as four cows once did. If animals receive timely vaccination and treatment, losses due to disease are reduced. In other words, healthier animals mean higher incomes for our livestock-rearing brothers and sisters.
Friends,
You are all familiar with the National Gokul Mission. Through it, indigenous breeds are being preserved and scientific breeding is being promoted. The new research centre established in Banaskantha will further strengthen this mission. Indigenous cattle breeds such as Gir, Sahiwal, and Kankrej, and buffalo breeds such as Mehsana, Murrah, and Jaffarabadi, will be preserved here. At the same time, major work will be done to improve their quality. For the Kankrej breed, this is the first facility of its kind in the country. Consider a farmer who owns a high-quality cow that produces more milk and remains healthy at a lower cost. Naturally, that farmer would want future generations of that cow to retain those same qualities. Modern technologies such as IVF help achieve exactly that. They increase the likelihood that superior traits will pass on to future generations. The direct benefit of this goes to livestock rearers.
Friends,
Protecting livestock from disease is also one of our priorities. Foot-and-mouth disease affects both animal health and milk production. Therefore, we launched a nationwide free vaccination campaign. So far, nearly 150 crore vaccine doses have been administered to animals. The livestock of more than eight crore farmers have received free vaccinations. This has also reduced the financial burden on livestock rearers.
Friends,
The impact of these efforts is visible in milk production as well. In 2013–14, a cow or buffalo produced on average less than five litres of milk per day. This was the situation when you sent me to Delhi. Less than five litres a day. Today, the national average has increased to around eight litres per day. India’s growth rate in milk productivity is the fastest in the world. India ranks number one globally in milk production. The benefits have reached villages, and the incomes of farming families have increased.
Friends,
We want livestock rearers to earn not only from milk but also from dung. Infrastructure is being developed for producing biogas, bio-CNG, and organic fertilisers from dung and agricultural residues. Institutions like Banas Dairy have an important role in this. Today, foundation stones have also been laid for two bio-CNG plants. Our objective is clear: healthier livestock, higher milk production, and complete utilisation of dung. We are transforming animal husbandry into not merely a tradition but also a strong means of increasing farmers’ incomes and enriching villages. I was interacting with the women here earlier. They told me they supply milk worth ₹2 crore. Milk worth ₹2 crore. Then I asked them how much education they had received. They replied, “Four books,” and yet they supply milk worth ₹2 crore.
Friends,
Over the past years, we have worked with a holistic approach for the prosperity of villages. Just look at the fisheries sector and see how much it has expanded. You will be pleased to know that India’s seafood exports have more than doubled. Our fishermen go out to sea, catch fish and shrimp, and sell them. Today, this sector has made enormous progress, and demand across the world has risen sharply. Cooperation in the fisheries sector is also being promoted.
Friends,
There is another sector that has provided an additional source of income for our farmers. That sector is beekeeping. Over the past twelve years, honey production has doubled. I remember that when I came to Banaskantha, I urged all of you to bring about a Sweet Revolution, a Honey Revolution. Today Banaskantha is setting new records in honey production. When I was interacting with the women earlier, they told me they sell honey worth ₹35 lakh. You will be proud to know that India has become the world's second-largest exporter of natural honey. In this Sweet Revolution, the contribution of our women’s self-help groups is also steadily increasing.
Friends,
A few days ago, on 7th October, I completed twenty-five years as head of government. It feels as though it happened only yesterday. Yes, it feels like yesterday itself, when I first took the oath on 7th October 2001. You all gave your Narendra Bhai immense affection and immense love.Today, I felt a little awkward here. Whatever is said in the rest of the country is one thing, but here Shankarbhai said, “Prime Minister Sahib, Prime Minister Sahib.” Tell me honestly, how will such an address go down my throat? Here, people habitually say, “Our Narendra Bhai has come.” Doesn't it feel better to say that? What joy is there in saying “Prime Minister Sahib”? And when my brothers from Gujarat say “Our Narendra Bhai,” my heart overflows with emotion. More than affection, every Gujarati taught me something. They guided me towards the right path and inspired me. At that time, I knew nothing about government offices, government functioning, or files. A person from an ordinary family, whose generations had never even dreamed of becoming the head of a village, was entrusted by you with the responsibility of serving first Gujarat and then the nation. Earlier while speaking with the women, they asked me how ideas such as Jyotigram, bringing water, natural farming, and initiatives for livestock came to me. I told them that there was no special formula. You taught me everything, and I simply went and implemented it.
Friends,
I have always known only two things: service to the people is service to the nation, and the development of Gujarat leads to the development of India. Everything else, how to work and how to move forward, you taught me. Whatever I have been able to do for the nation belongs to all the citizens of India, and to all of you as well. For this, I will remain indebted to you for my entire life. Until my final breath, I will remain devoted to service. Service, service, and service to the people of the country and to all of you.
Friends,
The senior citizens present here will still remember the old days. Twenty-five years ago, when I used to come here, there were severe problems of electricity and water. Even then, I used to say that we must save electricity and water. Farmers would protest against me, saying, “Who is Modi to tell us to save water? He won't even give us electricity.” I kept arguing with you, and eventually you accepted what I was saying. And today, just look at where we have come from and where we have reached. Those old problems now remain only in memories. Today, I will once again tell you the same thing: we must save water, and we must save electricity as well.
Friends,
The waters of the Narmada and modern technologies such as drip irrigation have transformed Banaskantha. They have changed both the face and the destiny of Banaskantha. Banaskantha’s potatoes are now world-famous. No one can come to a person from Banaskantha and say, “I will turn potatoes into gold,” because he will reply, “I am already doing that.” We have a cooperative brand like Banas Dairy here, which is expanding the cooperative movement to other parts of the country, including Kashi. I am especially grateful to Banas Dairy because even in my Kashi, people are benefiting from your experience and your service. Now, even the French fries potato processing plant has expanded its capacity. This will make it possible to purchase a larger quantity of potatoes. This is a major facility and support for potato farmers.
Friends,
A Cluster Development Programme is being implemented for farmers engaged in fruit and vegetable cultivation. Under this programme, twelve clusters have been approved today. These clusters are associated with fruits and vegetables such as tomatoes, potatoes, chillies, grapes, bananas, onions, oranges, pomegranates, and cocoa. Under this initiative, farmers will be supported in establishing new orchards and rejuvenating old ones. People will be trained and guided for the rejuvenation of older orchards, and subsidies will be provided for the entire project. The two clusters approved in North Gujarat will greatly benefit potato farmers of Banaskantha and Sabarkantha.
Friends,
Today, several other development projects related to Gujarat have also been inaugurated and launched. Gujarat has received two new railway services: the Ahmedabad–Varanasi Sabarmati Express and the Mehsana–Becharaji–Sabarmati MEMU train. Both are highly significant rail connectivity projects. In addition, the Ahmedabad Metro service is also being expanded. Today, the foundation stone has been laid for metro projects connecting GIFT City and the airport. The Ahmedabad–Mehsana Highway is now set to be expanded from four lanes to eight lanes.
Friends,
Today, more than 4,000 modern Anganwadis are also being inaugurated for the children of Gujarat. Nearly four lakh children and pregnant mothers will benefit from them.
Friends,
Every such effort is aimed at making India a developed nation. Today, every farmer, every young person, and every daughter and sister in the country is moving forward with the resolve of building a Developed India. But unfortunately, some people do not like this. Some people are unable to accept it. These are people who want to see the country in difficulty. They derive satisfaction from seeing the nation in trouble. Whenever challenges arise for the country, they feel happy.
Friends,
A recent example of this is the war taking place around Iran and the Gulf region. At a time when India is united in dealing with its consequences, these people were busy spreading rumours. Rumours were spread among farmers that fertilisers would not be available. Artificial queues were created and the atmosphere was disturbed. Women were frightened by being told that cooking gas would no longer be available, asking them how they would cook food and how their children would go to school. Their plan was to create panic and disorder in the country so that they could defame Modi.
Friends,
I want to remind the farmer brothers and sisters of this country that I had said Modi would stand firmly with you. And you can see that even though the war is still continuing, Modi did not allow any shortage of fertilisers for farmers. We did not allow fertiliser supplies to run short.
Friends,
Because of this war, fertiliser prices around the world have risen sharply. The chemicals used in producing fertilisers have also become much more expensive. Yet the government did not allow this burden to fall on farmers. A bag of urea that costs around ₹3,000 elsewhere in the world is available to Indian farmers for less than ₹300. The global price of a bag of urea is around ₹3,000, but the government bears that burden and provides it to you for around ₹300. The price of a bag of DAP fertiliser has crossed ₹5,000 globally. But Indian farmers receive the same bag for around ₹1,350. The nation is providing this support so that our farmers become stronger and their lives improve.
Friends,
In a world full of uncertainty, India’s rapid development has become a new source of hope for the entire world. In such a situation, we must continue moving forward on the path of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat - One India, Great India. And tomorrow, the 31st of October, is a day to strengthen this resolve. Tomorrow is the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and National Unity Day. The entire nation will celebrate National Unity Day. On this day, the Run for Unity is organised across the country. Reports are coming in from all directions about the grand preparations being made for the Run for Unity. I would especially urge all citizens of the country, particularly our young friends, to participate enthusiastically in the Run for Unity tomorrow morning.
Friends,
Every year, the Unity Festival is celebrated in Ekta Nagar on the morning of 31st October. But this year, keeping the Run for Unity and other programmes in mind, it will be held in the evening instead of the morning. This is a change from previous years. Tomorrow at 5:30 in the evening, a grand Unity Festival will be celebrated in Ekta Nagar. The programme will be organised on a very large scale. You should watch it on television. There will be such a parade on the soil of Gujarat that it will remind you of the Republic Day celebrations in Delhi. Do watch it. There will be parades by police and security forces, and impressive tableaux will be displayed. I urge all citizens of the country to join this programme tomorrow evening as well. From Kashmir to Kanyakumari, from Kutch to Kamakhya, the entire nation should pay tribute to Sardar Patel and reaffirm the resolve of Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat. With this appeal, I once again extend my best wishes to all of you for these development works.
Thank you very much.
The sisters seated at the back are offering their blessings to me. Mothers, I bow at your feet. Your blessings give me tremendous strength. I am deeply grateful to all of you.
Bharat Mata Ki Jai!
Bharat Mata Ki Jai!

title: India to Host ICAR- CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027 in New Delhi from April 12–17; Over 5,000 Delegates Expected to participate
subtitle:
CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027 to Showcase India's Agricultural Transformation and Global Research Partnerships

CGIAR and ICAR to bring their work in India closer together around national priorities: Dr M L Jat

India to Promote South-South Cooperation and Share Agricultural Innovations with Global South: Dr. M. L. Jat

India–CGIAR Partnership Demonstrates the Transformative Power of Science and Technology: Dr. Ismahane Elouafi

Science, Technology and Global Partnerships Have Transformed India's Agricultural Landscape: Dr. Himanshu Pathak
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 2:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
CGIAR and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) today announced that New Delhi will host
CGIAR Science and Partnership Week
from 12th  to 17th April 2027. The event is organized by ICAR, of the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India, and CGIAR.
The week will bring researchers, farmers, governments, startups and businesses from around the world to New Delhi. Together, they will look at the innovations already reaching farmers and where more work is needed to reach many more.
India is a natural host. ICAR leads one of the world’s largest national agricultural research systems, and its scientists have worked with CGIAR for more than 50 years. Ten CGIAR research centers now work in India, on crops, water, livestock, fish, nutrition, and policy.
India’s agricultural science also reaches well beyond its borders. A groundnut sample from India, conserved and shared by ICRISAT, contributed to varieties now grown in Malawi, Uganda, Mozambique, and Zambia. Hyderabad’s Center of Excellence for South–South Cooperation in Agriculture shares proven farming innovations across Asia, Africa, and Latin America.
Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, DARE and Director General, ICAR highlighted the longstanding partnership between India and CGIAR, which has played a significant role in strengthening agricultural research and development in the country for over five decades.
He noted that CGIAR, an international agricultural research partnership comprising 15 research centres working across more than 100 countries, has contributed significantly to global agricultural advancement. Its collaboration with India, particularly through ICAR, has supported important developments in crop improvement, natural resource management, food security and agricultural productivity
Referring to India's agricultural transformation since the Green Revolution, Dr. Jat highlighted how collaboration with international research institutions, including CIMMYT, IRRI and ICRISAT, contributed to strengthening India's food production capabilities. From a food-deficit nation dependent on imports, India has emerged as a major food-producing and exporting country.
He emphasised that the CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027 will provide an important platform to strengthen international cooperation and facilitate the exchange of scientific knowledge, technologies and best practices.
Dr. Jat stated that India's priority would be to promote South-South cooperation and share its successful agricultural innovations with the Global South, particularly African countries. He highlighted India's progress in climate-resilient agriculture, digital agriculture and AgriStack, agricultural mechanisation, millets, natural farming and sustainable agricultural practices as areas offering considerable opportunities for international collaboration.
He further noted that the event would deliberate on emerging priorities across the agri-food value chain, including climate resilience, water management, soil health, public-private partnerships, startups, youth and women's participation, and the role of media in communicating agricultural science and innovations.
Dr. Ismahane Elouafi, Executive Managing Director, CGIAR, emphasised that the upcoming event would celebrate the achievements of this longstanding partnership while developing a forward-looking agenda for the next 50 years of agricultural cooperation. She highlighted that India has shown what strong national science can achieve at scale. Seed and knowledge from India already help farmers in Africa and Asia. In April, we want to build on that exchange and consider together where science can do more, she added.
She also underscored the importance of recognising the contribution of science and scientists in improving human well-being and strengthening food systems. Referring to the successful first edition held in Nairobi, Kenya, in April 2025, she expressed confidence that the India edition would further strengthen global partnerships and bring together stakeholders to develop solutions for emerging agricultural challenges.
Dr. Himanshu Pathak, Director General, ICRISAT  says “India's agricultural journey from a food-deficit nation to a major food-producing and exporting country reflects the transformative power of science, technology and international partnerships. Through CGIAR Science and Partnership Week 2027, we aim to showcase India's agricultural achievements, share our innovations with the world and learn from global advancements to co-create solutions for the emerging challenges of agriculture and food systems.”
The first CGIAR Science Week took place in Nairobi, Kenya, in April 2025, where CGIAR launched its current research portfolio. The New Delhi edition will focus on how we move from science to impact and how partnership can advance South–South cooperation. It will also explore how agricultural research and innovation can contribute to India’s vision for 2047.
The program and speakers will be announced in the coming months.

title: Ministry of Coal Holds Stakeholder Consultation on ‘Mining for Future’; Urges Allottees to Bring Allocated Coal Blocks into Production Faster
subtitle: Of 137 commercial mines allocated since 2020, 25 are producing; Ministry seeks industry inputs to close the gap
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Coal today held a Stakeholder Consultation on ‘Mining for Future’ in Panjim, Goa. The day-long consultation brought together allottees of captive and commercial coal blocks, representatives of State Governments, CGWA, DGH, MoEFCC and senior officials of the Ministry to discuss faster operationalisation of allocated blocks, the next set of policy reforms, and responsible mining.
\
Shri Vikram Dev Dutt, Secretary, Ministry of Coal, was the Chief Guest. Smt. Rupinder Brar, Additional Secretary & Nominated Authority and senior officials of the Ministry were present.
The main message of the consultation was that India’s next gains in coal production will come from allocating new blocks as well as more from bringing already allocated blocks into production. Addressing the allottees, the Secretary said, “A block that is allocated but not producing is capacity the country has set aside and cannot use.”
The Secretary said the past eight months had tested the sector. When the conflict in West Asia disrupted LNG and LPG supplies from late February, coal stocks at mines and power plants allowed the Government to assure the country of steady power, and he thanked the industry for that. He cautioned that the pressure has not eased. The International Energy Agency expects gas markets to stay tight through 2027. Asian spot LNG averaged US$17.5 per MBtu in the second quarter, 45% higher than a year earlier, global coal demand is forecast at a record 8.94 billion tonnes in 2026. “Each tonne we produce at home protects the economy from these swings,” the Secretary said.
He added that domestic demand points the same way. NITI Aayog projects coal demand rising from about 1.25 billion tonnes in 2025 to over 2.6 billion tonnes by 2050 under current policies, and above 1.8 billion tonnes even on a net zero path, as steel, cement and power, the three largest consumers, expand several times over. India produced 1,041 million tonnes of coal in FY 2025-26, and coal still supplies more than 70% of its electricity.
Shri Dutt further elaborated that the Ministry’s commitments span multiple dimensions, including sustainability, community welfare, and technological advancement. He emphasised the importance of scientific mine closure, highlighting the need to transform mined-out areas into co-created, vibrant habitats that promote a harmonious ecosystem, ensuring ecological restoration alongside community well-being and long-term social stability. He said that CSR initiatives have been instrumental in bringing positive change in coal-bearing regions and must continue to be strengthened so that communities feel included and benefit from development initiatives.
Smt. Rupinder Brar, Additional Secretary, took participants through the reforms carried out so far. The 2020 framework removed end-use restrictions, moved bidding to a revenue share linked to the National Coal Index, dropped technical and financial eligibility conditions, and allowed 100% FDI through the automatic route, with underground mines getting a waiver of the upfront amount, a lower floor price and lower performance security. Scheduled operationalisation has since been cut from 51 to 40 months for fully explored blocks and from 66 to 52 months for partially explored ones. Mining plan approvals now average 4.5 months against 9 earlier, Mine Opening Permission is granted by the company Board, and 44 accredited exploration agencies no longer need a prospecting licence.
She thanked the efforts taken by different ministries for the reforms taken for faster operationalization of coal blocks. She called for accelerated coal production with a conscious approach, balancing growth with environmental stewardship and community well-being underscoring that sustainability must move in tandem with scale. Highlighting the transformational impact of coal sector reforms, she emphasised transparency, policy stability, and ease of doing business as key drivers attracting investment, fostering competition, and unlocking new economic avenues
The Ministry asked allottees to open mines ahead of the revised timelines, ramp up to peak rated capacity quickly, raise land, forest and State-level issues early, and mine responsibly. It also sought their suggestions on policy changes that would speed up operationalisation, clauses in coal mine agreements that need revisiting, and amendments required in Acts and Rules. On responsible mining, the Secretary said a mine takes land, draws on water and changes livelihoods. Families who give up land should know from day one what they will receive, where they will move and how their incomes will be restored, and companies should honour every commitment they make.
The stakeholder consultation witnessed insightful deliberations across key sessions covering critical dimensions of coal sector transformation. Discussions focused on future of mining like Underground Coal Gasification, technology adoption, innovation to drive efficiency and value addition; inclusive growth through rehabilitation, resettlement, land repurposing, worker welfare, CSR and just transition with communities and all stakeholders at the centre; and sustainability measures promoting greener mining practices and environmental stewardship. Together, the sessions reflected a holistic roadmap for a modern, responsible, future-ready and self-reliant coal sector.
On technology, industry presented advances in AI, robotics and digital transformation, reducing ash in coal at the mine, underground coal gasification, modern exploration techniques and paste filling, along with global best practices. Officials of DGH, DGMS, MoEF&CC and CGWA spoke on the CBM framework, mine safety, environmental policy reforms and groundwater clearance, followed by an open house on policy enablement and the next generation of reforms. Participants also discussed mine closure, CSR and community welfare in mining regions, afforestation and environmental stewardship, and shared experiences on the impact of policy reforms, first mile connectivity and ways to increase coking coal production.

title: Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Chairs Chintan Shivir on Digitisation of Trade
subtitle:
Discussions Focus on Empowering Kirana Retailers through Digital Procurement and Supply-Chain Efficiency

DigiDukaan Connects Over 21,000 Retailers with More Than 450 Brands Across Three Cities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 8:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal chaired the Bharat Commerce Chintan Shivir, a high-level CEO Roundtable convened by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) and the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi. The roundtable brought together over 40 leaders from leading Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) companies to deliberate on a shared roadmap for strengthening and digitising India's General Trade ecosystem through ONDC DigiDukaan.
Speaking at the roundtable, Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal said, “ONDC’s DigiDukaan shows that when open digital infrastructure is built around the needs of the small retailer, adoption follows. Let this become another case study where the world can learn from India. By making procurement simpler and more transparent while strengthening our distributors, we can help kiranas free up working capital and grow. I invite the FMCG industry to work together and take this to every corner of Bharat.”
Shri Amardeep Singh Bhatia, Secretary, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) said, “Open digital infrastructure has a critical role to play in accelerating the digitalisation of India’s retail ecosystem, particularly its vast network of kirana stores. ONDC’s DigiDukaan is an important step in this direction, demonstrating how an open, interoperable network can enable neighbourhood retailers to access digital procurement opportunities and participate more effectively in the evolving digital economy. By bringing together retailers, FMCG companies and distributors on a common network, DPIIT along with ONDC is helping build a more connected and efficient General Trade ecosystem, creating a pathway for digitalisation to reach kiranas at scale.”
The discussions focused on strengthening and re-empowering the General Trade ecosystem, which remains central to India's retail economy and supports the livelihoods of millions of neighbourhood retailers. Participants emphasised the need for greater institutional commitment from FMCG companies, distributors and industry stakeholders to accelerate digital procurement, improve supply-chain efficiency and enhance the competitiveness of kirana stores. The initiative seeks to bring industry stakeholders together through common digital infrastructure, shared services and commercially sustainable models.
Senior representatives from Hindustan Unilever (HUL), Coca-Cola India, ITC, P&G, Marico, CavinKare, Pidilite, Britannia, Adani Wilmar, LT Foods, Anmol Industries, Haldiram's, Emami, Veeba and Nilon's participated in the roundtable, along with representatives from logistics providers, technology partners and ONDC network participants.
ONDC DigiDukaan addresses procurement by digitising kiranas as buyers. Through a single digital interface, retailers can discover and order products across multiple brands, distributors and wholesalers, with greater visibility into pricing, trade schemes and product availability. The initiative is designed to strengthen existing distribution relationships rather than replace them, while creating a common digital foundation through which retailers can eventually access shared logistics, formal credit and other services. This approach seeks to reduce the complexity and cost of participation across the General Trade value chain.
The roundtable deliberated on five key areas for strengthening the General Trade ecosystem. These included developing a common digital identity for kirana retailers to enable seamless engagement with multiple brands, distributors and service providers; creating shared logistics and micro-warehousing infrastructure to improve distributor reach and facilitate reliable next-day replenishment, including in areas beyond existing delivery routes; and expanding access to formal credit through financing solutions linked to digital procurement and transaction activity to improve access to working capital and reduce dependence on informal distributor credit.
Discussions also focused on simplifying technology integration through plug-and-play Distributor Management System (DMS) connectors, standardised catalogues and common digital interfaces to reduce onboarding complexity and encourage wider industry participation. Participants further deliberated on realigning commercial incentives for FMCG companies, sales teams, distributors and channel partners to make digital ordering, wider retail coverage and sustained retailer adoption commercially beneficial across the value chain.
DigiDukaan has connected over 21,000 retailers with more than 450 brands across Hyderabad, Jaipur and Mumbai as of September 2026, compared with over 12,000 retailers in the previous quarter. In Hyderabad, more than 16,000 retailers have been onboarded, with monthly repeat ordering rates of 73–78%. An initial ONDC retailer study also found that 40% of surveyed retailers reported lower inventory holdings for products procured through DigiDukaan, indicating the potential for improved working capital efficiency.
The National Traders' Welfare Board (NTWB), under the chairmanship of Shri Sunil J. Singhi, has been working closely with ONDC to accelerate the adoption of DigiDukaan among kirana retailers. The collaboration focuses on mobilising local trade associations, strengthening retailer participation and enabling small businesses to benefit from digital procurement and more efficient distribution networks.
Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, ONDC, Shri Vibhor Jain, said, “Digital adoption for the distributor fraternity has been developing - billing, printing, order placement are largely online. But retailers, most of which are mom-and-pop shops, still run on pen, paper and memory. DigiDukaan is ONDC's effort to build digital infrastructure for India's General Trade ecosystem in retail. We are digitising kiranas as buyers, while strengthening the existing distributor network rather than replacing it.”
DigiDukaan is building an expanding network of FMCG brands, technology providers and logistics partners. Leading FMCG companies, including HUL, Marico, Colgate-Palmolive, Emami and Amul, are participating through their distribution networks, while ITC, Tata Consumer Products and Britannia are at various stages of integration or discussion. On the technology front, Paytm for Business, Qwipo and Mulltiply.ai are live on the network, while DMS and technology providers, including Bizom, Botree, QuIDPe and ENS, are progressing towards integration. Logistics and warehousing partners, including ElasticRun, Shiprocket, India Post and Moeving, are also part of the expanding ecosystem, supporting seamless procurement, wider distributor reach and faster replenishment for kirana retailers.
As part of its next phase, ONDC is focusing on deepening brand and distributor participation in Mumbai, particularly North Mumbai, while strengthening operations across existing markets.
The Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) is building open digital commerce infrastructure in India through a network model aimed at reducing entry barriers and improving access for businesses. The network has enabled over 500 million transactions to date, with retail as its core focus area. It seeks to create digital networks that improve efficiency, lower costs and unlock opportunities for businesses, gig workers, small retailers and consumers.
ONDC-enabled retail initiatives include DigiDukaan, which has onboarded over 21,000 retailers for business-to-business (B2B) procurement digitisation, and Amazing India, which focuses on enabling products from kisans, karigars, cooperatives and other micro-producers to become e-commerce-ready and reach wider markets.
Other initiatives include public transport services, facilitating over 5 lakh metro and bus journeys daily through more than 40 consumer applications; logistics infrastructure used by over 80,000 merchants and 30+ small and micro fleet operators; and more than 1,000 tourism experiences, including 170 Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) monuments and 29 museums, available on the network. ONDC has also enabled low-ticket investment and credit solutions aimed at expanding financial access, with a majority of investors coming from Tier-2 cities and beyond.

title: Government Ensures Continuity of Telecom Connectivity amid Cyclone Arnab
subtitle:
Telecom restoration efforts underway in affected districts through coordinated action by telecom service providers

Intra-Circle Roaming operational across affected districts of Andhra Pradesh; 11 Cell on Wheels deployed to support connectivity
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 10:17PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), in coordination with Telecom Service Providers (TSPs), is undertaking restoration efforts and monitoring the telecom network situation to ensure the continuity of essential communication services in the affected areas, after Cyclone Arnab hit along the coast of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. Widespread heavy rainfall, flash floods, tree falls and power infrastructure disruptions affected telecom services across parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and adjoining regions.
Significant progress has been achieved in restoring network connectivity across Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, with particular focus on resolving power supply disruptions and restoring optical fibre connectivity. Emergency connectivity arrangements, including ICR and COW deployments, are being maintained to facilitate uninterrupted communication for citizens and support relief and restoration activities in the affected regions.
In Andhra Pradesh, overall telecom network availability has reached 99.18 percent. Among the affected districts, network availability stands at 98.5 per cent in West Godavari, 91.96 per cent in Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Konaseema. Commercial power supply disruptions and localised Optical Fibre Cable (OFC) cuts are the primary factors affecting network operations. Intra-Circle Roaming (ICR) remains operational across affected districts to facilitate connectivity for subscribers, irrespective of their service provider. Additionally, 11 Cell on Wheels (COWs) have been deployed to strengthen emergency communication services.
In Odisha, following Cyclone ARNAB, the telecom network situation in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts has been gradually improving with the easing of rainfall and receding of floodwaters. Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) have initiated restoration work at affected sites, resulting in progressive improvement in network connectivity and a reduction in service disruptions. All TSPs are making sustained efforts on a priority basis to restore the remaining affected sites and ensure early normalisation of telecom services and uninterrupted connectivity for the public.
What is ICR & how to use it:
Intra Circle Roaming (ICR) is a telecom arrangement where a mobile subscriber connects to another operator’s (TSP’s) network within the same telecom circle (region). This allows users to access mobile services even if their own operator (TSP) has no coverage in that specific area. It plays a critical role during natural disasters when mobile infrastructure is damaged.
During the time of disaster, if mobile infrastructure is damaged in a region, DoT issues instructions to Telecom Service Providers to implement ICR.
To ensure ICR works:
Keep "Automatic Network Selection" enabled in your phone settings.
If automatic connection fails;
Go to Settings > Mobile Networks > Network Operators
Manually select another available network

In a significant step towards strengthening digital infrastructure and accelerating broadband connectivity across rural Tamil Nadu, Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) under Department of Telecommunications (DoT) signed a Utilisation Agreement for connecting the rural households under Amended BharatNet Program (ABP) in the State under the State-led model today at Sanchar Bhawan, New Delhi.
The Agreement was signed between Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), DoT; Government of Tamil Nadu; and Tamil Nadu FibreNet Corporation (TANFINET) for Utilisation of BharatNet Network in Tamil Nadu under ABP.
The Agreement signing ceremony was held in the august presence of Shri Shyamal Misra, Administrator, Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN), Department of Telecommunications. V. Vallidevi, General Manager (Projects), Tamil Nadu FibreNet Corporation and Shri Dinesh Kumar Garg, DDG (ABP Implementation-I), Department of Telecommunications, along with senior officers of DoT, DBN and BSNL.
The Union Cabinet had approved the Amended BharatNet Program on 4th August 2023 with the objective of upgrading, consolidating and expanding the existing BharatNet network to ensure robust and future-ready broadband connectivity to all Gram Panchayats and villages on demand basis.
The Government of India has approved financial subsidy support for utilisation of BharatNet network under Amended BharatNet Program. The initiative is expected to facilitate more than five lakh rural home fibre connections in the state of Tamil Nadu with financial support from the Government of India and significantly enhance delivery of digital services including e-Governance, online education, telemedicine, digital payments and citizen-centric services across rural and remote areas of the State. Digital Bharat Nidhi (erstwhile USOF) was established under the Indian Telegraph (Amendment) Act, 2003 w.e.f. 01.04.2002. As per ‘The Telecommunications Act, 2023’ the Universal Service Obligation Fund, has become the Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN). The DBN has mandate to support universal service through promoting access and delivery of telecommunication service in underserved rural, remote and urban areas. It is an attached office of the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications.
In order to achieve objectives of DBN, it covers various schemes and projects including BharatNet, 4G Saturation Project, Provision of Mobile Service in uncovered areas of Aspirational Districts, Mobile Services in Left Wing Extremist Areas, Mobile Services in Himalayan and Border areas, Mobile Services in Islands and Mobile Services in North Eastern Areas.

The guidelines are anchored in seven guiding sutras or principles — Trust is the Foundation, People First, Innovation over Restraint, Fairness & Equity, Accountability, Understandable by Design, and Safety, Resilience & Sustainability.  Part 4 of the guidelines provides practical guidance for industry actors and regulators to increase clarity, predictability and accountability in the ecosystem.
The telecommunication sector constitutes a significant part of India’s digital infrastructure. Today, the telecommunication sector supports connectivity for the public, delivery of public and essential e-services, conduct of trade and commerce, and secure and resilient functioning of the country’s critical information infrastructure. It is critical not only for social, economic and commercial activities but also for national security and emergency response in the country.
At present, AI is increasingly being integrated into telecommunication networks and provision of telecommunication services. With a view to ensuring consistent and responsible implementation of the India AI Governance Guidelines in the telecommunication sector, and to increase clarity, predictability and accountability in the ecosystem, TRAI has decided to frame guidelines on responsible use of AI in telecommunication networks and provision of telecommunication services after following stakeholders’ consultation.
