title: Holy Relics of Lord Buddha to be Exposed for Public Veneration in Arunachal Pradesh from 31 October to 21 November 2026
subtitle:
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, to participate in the inaugural ceremony at Tawang on 31 October 2026

Sacred Piprahwa Relics from the National Museum, New Delhi, to be taken to Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai, reflecting Arunachal Pradesh's rich Buddhist traditions

Special Indian Air Force aircraft and helicopter arrangements planned for the safe and dignified transportation of the Holy Relics

Exhibition on the discovery and repatriation of the Piprahwa heritage to accompany the exposition at all three locations

International conference on “Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond” to bring together monks, scholars and delegates from India and six other countries
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 10:35AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, the International Buddhist Confederation (IBC) and the National Museum, New Delhi, is organising an exposition of the Holy Relics of Shakyamuni Buddha in Arunachal Pradesh from
31 October to 21 November 2026
. The exposition will cover three important centres of Buddhist faith and heritage—Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai, providing devotees and members of the public an opportunity to pay homage to the Sacred Relics.
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, is scheduled to participate in the inaugural ceremony at the historic Gaden Namgyal Lhatse (Tawang Monastery) on
31 October 2026
. The programme will be attended by distinguished representatives of the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, venerable members of the Buddhist Sangha, representatives of Buddhist institutions, devotees and other dignitaries.
The exposition is being organised in recognition of the deep spiritual significance of the Holy Relics and Arunachal Pradesh's distinctive place in India's Buddhist cultural landscape. It also reflects the Government of India's continuing commitment to the protection, preservation and dissemination of the country's Buddhist heritage, and to strengthening cultural and spiritual connections with Buddhist communities in India and abroad.
Tawang Monastery
Ceremonial Movement and Inauguration at Tawang
The Holy Relics, presently preserved at the National Museum, New Delhi, will commence their sacred journey with ceremonial observances at the Museum on the night of
30 October 2026
. They will thereafter be taken to Air Force Station Palam for onward transportation to Arunachal Pradesh.
As per the proposed movement itinerary, the Holy Relics are scheduled to depart from Palam in the early hours of
31 October 2026
by a special Indian Air Force aircraft and reach Air Force Station Borjhar, Guwahati, before being transported by helicopter to Tawang.
Upon arrival, the Holy Relics will be received with due religious ceremony and reverence. They will thereafter be taken to Tawang Monastery for installation and the inaugural ceremony, scheduled between
10:00 AM and 11:30 AM on 31 October 2026
.
A further inaugural function, together with the opening of the associated exposition and exhibition, is scheduled for
1 November 2026
, with the Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh, Shri Pema Khandu, as the Chief Guest.
The occasion coincides with the observance of
Lhabab Düchen
, a significant festival in the Tibetan Buddhist tradition commemorating the Buddha's descent from the heavenly realm. The exposition will thus bring together religious observance, cultural heritage and public participation in a spiritually meaningful setting.
The movement and installation of the Holy Relics are being planned with particular attention to their sanctity, security and conservation requirements. The Ministry of Culture is coordinating with the Ministry of Defence, Indian Air Force, Government of Arunachal Pradesh, National Museum and other concerned agencies for the necessary operational arrangements.
Bomdila Monastery
Exposition Schedule: Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai
The Holy Relics will be available for public darshan at the following locations:
Dates
Venue
Programme
31 October 2026
Gaden Namgyal Lhatse, Tawang Monastery
Arrival, ceremonial reception and inaugural ceremony
1–7 November 2026
Tawang Monastery
Public darshan and exposition
8–13 November 2026
TGL Monastery (Lower Gompa), Bomdila
Public darshan and exposition
14–20 November 2026
Golden Pagoda, Namsai
Public darshan and exposition
21 November 2026
Namsai–Tezu–New Delhi
Ceremonial departure and return of the Holy Relics to the National Museum
On
8 November
, the Holy Relics are scheduled to travel from Tawang to Rupa by helicopter and thereafter by road to Bomdila. The itinerary includes ceremonial reception at Upper Gompa before their installation at Lower Gompa, where the inaugural ceremony is scheduled between 3:00 PM and 4:00 PM.
On
14 November
, the Holy Relics will be transported from Bomdila to Rupa by road and thereafter by helicopter to Nalung Helipad, Namsai. They will be taken to the Golden Pagoda, where the installation and inaugural ceremony are scheduled between 11:00 AM and 12:00 noon.
Following the conclusion of public darshan at Namsai, the Holy Relics are scheduled to return to the National Museum, New Delhi, on
21 November 2026
, via Tezu Airport and Air Force Station Palam.
The timings and movement arrangements will remain subject to operational, weather and security considerations.
Namsai Pagoda
Sacred Piprahwa Relics: An Extraordinary Archaeological and Spiritual Heritage
The Holy Relics being taken to Arunachal Pradesh originate from
Piprahwa in present-day Siddharthnagar district, Uttar Pradesh
, an archaeological site associated with ancient Kapilavastu and the Shakya tradition of Lord Buddha.
Piprahwa occupies a prominent place in the archaeological history of Buddhism. In
1898
, William Claxton Peppé excavated a stupa at the site and discovered reliquaries containing bone fragments and precious objects, bringing international attention to the historical and religious significance of the discovery.
Subsequently, the Archaeological Survey of India conducted further excavations between
1971 and 1977
, under the supervision of archaeologist Shri K. M. Srivastava. Excavations at deeper levels revealed two additional reliquary caskets containing ancient bone relics traditionally associated with Lord Buddha.
The larger casket contained
12 sacred bone fragments
, while the smaller casket contained
10
, making a total of
22 sacred relics
recovered during these excavations. Of these, 20 are preserved at the National Museum, New Delhi, and two at the Indian Museum, Kolkata.
The relics, comprising ancient osteological material, are regarded as exceptionally rare and are accorded profound religious reverence by Buddhist communities. Their historical and archaeological importance is accompanied by a deep spiritual significance rooted in the long-established Buddhist tradition of relic veneration.
Following the Mahāparinirvāṇa of Lord Buddha at Kushinagar, the tradition of enshrining His corporeal relics in stupas developed into an important expression of Buddhist devotion. Over the centuries, these sacred sites became centres of pilgrimage, religious learning and cultural exchange.
The present exposition offers devotees an opportunity to connect with this ancient spiritual tradition while also drawing attention to the importance of preserving archaeological and religious heritage for future generations.
Arunachal Pradesh: A Meeting Place of Buddhist Traditions
Arunachal Pradesh occupies a distinctive position in the Buddhist cultural geography of India. Its monasteries, religious institutions and living traditions reflect historical connections with the wider Himalayan region and other parts of Buddhist Asia.
The western and northern parts of the State, including Tawang and West Kameng, are particularly associated with the Mahāyāna and Vajrayāna traditions of Himalayan Buddhism.
Tawang Monastery, also known as Gaden Namgyal Lhatse, is an important centre of monastic learning, religious practice and cultural continuity. The monasteries of Bomdila similarly sustain the spiritual and artistic traditions of the region.
In eastern Arunachal Pradesh, particularly Namsai and adjoining areas, the Theravāda traditions followed by the Tai Khamti and other Buddhist communities represent another important dimension of India's diverse Buddhist heritage.
The exposition across Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai will therefore bring the Holy Relics to communities representing different Buddhist traditions, reflecting the diversity and shared spiritual foundations of Buddhism within the State.
Beyond its religious significance, the initiative is expected to strengthen awareness of Arunachal Pradesh's Buddhist heritage, encourage cultural exchange and promote the universal values of peace, compassion, non-violence and harmony associated with the teachings of Lord Buddha.
Government of India's Continuing Commitment to Buddhist Heritage
Under the leadership of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government of India has undertaken initiatives for the conservation, protection, promotion and international dissemination of India's Buddhist heritage.
These efforts include the preservation of Buddhist monuments and sacred objects, development of pilgrimage infrastructure, support for Buddhist scholarship and cultural exchanges, recovery of important heritage objects and organisation of international expositions of Sacred Relics.
The Government's approach recognises the importance of safeguarding India's civilisational inheritance while strengthening the cultural and spiritual relationships that connect India with Buddhist communities across the world.
A significant recent development was the return to India in
2025 of the Piprahwa jewel collection
, associated with the historic 1898 discovery. Following the proposed international auction of the collection, the Ministry of Culture undertook efforts that contributed to its return after approximately 127 years.
The homecoming of these precious objects marked an important development in the preservation and recovery of India's cultural heritage and renewed public interest in the history of Piprahwa and the early Buddhist tradition.
The Government of India's initiatives also reflect the broader principle of
“Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”
, emphasising the complementary importance of development and preservation of heritage.
International Expositions: Strengthening India's Buddhist Cultural Connections
India has a longstanding tradition of sharing its sacred Buddhist heritage through international relic expositions, enabling devotees abroad to participate in public veneration and reinforcing historical bonds of friendship.
Over the decades, Government of India-supported expositions have taken place in countries including Sri Lanka, Mongolia, Singapore, the Republic of Korea and Thailand.
In recent years, such initiatives have continued to strengthen cultural diplomacy and people-to-people relations.
In
2022
, the exposition of the Holy Relics of Lord Buddha in Mongolia reaffirmed the longstanding Buddhist connections between India and Mongolia.
In
2024
, the Holy Relics of Lord Buddha, together with the relics of His two principal disciples, Arahant Sariputta and Arahant Mahamoggallana, were taken to Thailand for public veneration at Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Ubon Ratchathani and Krabi. The exposition witnessed participation by millions of devotees.
In
2025
, the Holy Relics of Lord Buddha were taken to Vietnam during the Vesak celebrations, attracting widespread public participation. Expositions were also undertaken in Kalmykia, Russia, and Bhutan, further strengthening India's spiritual and cultural ties with Buddhist communities in these regions.
In
February 2026
, the sacred Devnimori Relics were taken to Sri Lanka for public veneration, reflecting the enduring Buddhist relationship between the two countries.
In
May 2026
, the exposition of the Holy Relics of Lord Buddha in Ladakh provided devotees and monastic communities of the Himalayan region an important opportunity for collective prayer and reverence.
Subsequently, during
May–June 2026
, the Holy Relics of Arahant Sariputta and Arahant Mahamoggallana from Sanchi were taken to Mongolia for a special exposition at the Gandan Tegchenling Monastery in Ulaanbaatar.
These initiatives demonstrate India's commitment to sharing its Buddhist heritage in a spirit of mutual respect, cultural understanding and spiritual fellowship.
The exposition in Arunachal Pradesh represents another important step in this continuing engagement, bringing the sacred heritage preserved at the National Museum closer to Buddhist communities in India's northeastern Himalayan region.
Special Exhibition: “Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa”
As an important accompanying initiative, the International Buddhist Confederation will organise an exhibition titled “Unearthing the Sacred Piprahwa: The Story of the Holy Buddha Relics and Their Discovery” at Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai.
The exhibition will present the historical and spiritual significance of Buddhist relic veneration, beginning with the life and teachings of Siddhartha Gautama and the development of the tradition of enshrining Sacred Relics following His Mahāparinirvāṇa.
It will trace the archaeological discoveries at Piprahwa, including the excavation undertaken by William Claxton Peppé in 1898 and the subsequent investigations by the Archaeological Survey of India.
The exhibition will also examine the historical journey of the Piprahwa jewels, their association with the Peppé family collection, the proposed international auction in 2025 and the subsequent efforts that led to their return to India.
Through this narrative, visitors will gain an understanding of the relationship between archaeological research, religious traditions, heritage preservation and the recovery of culturally significant objects.
The exhibition is expected to serve as an important educational and cultural component of the exposition, particularly for students, scholars, young visitors and members of the public interested in India's Buddhist history.
International Conference on “Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond”
The International Buddhist Confederation, in collaboration with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh, will also organise an international conference titled “Buddhism: Dissemination in the Himalayan Region and Beyond” at the Kalawangpo Convention Hall, Tawang, on 2 November 2026.
The conference is expected to bring together venerable monks, Buddhist scholars and delegates from India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Malaysia, Indonesia and Germany.
It will provide a platform for scholarly dialogue on the historical transmission of Buddhist teachings, the evolution of monastic institutions, the preservation of Buddhist knowledge traditions and the contemporary relevance of Buddhist philosophy and ethical principles.
The deliberations will be organised around three broad themes:
1. Carrying Forward the Buddha's Legacy after Mahāparinirvāṇa
This theme will examine the continuity of Buddhist teachings and practices following the Mahāparinirvāṇa of Lord Buddha. Discussions will cover the Four Noble Truths as a living heritage, conservation and material culture, the evolution of religious institutions, international engagement through Sacred Relic expositions and Buddhism's contribution to shared cultural traditions.
2. Historical and Doctrinal Continuity of Buddhism
This theme will focus on the intergenerational transmission of Buddhist textual and monastic lineages, with particular reference to Arunachal Pradesh. It will also explore the plurality of Buddhist schools, shared doctrinal foundations, language and interpretation, pedagogical traditions, and the preservation of Buddhist ideas through art and cultural expression.
3. Buddhism and Right Livelihood
The third theme will explore the contemporary relevance of Buddhist ethical teachings, including connections between the intellectual traditions of Nalanda and modern academia, cultural tourism and pilgrimage, skill development, sustainable livelihoods, and the relationship between Buddhism, globalisation and consumerism.
The conference will highlight Arunachal Pradesh's importance as a living centre of Buddhist heritage, where diverse traditions have been sustained through monastic institutions, community practices and cultural exchange.
It will also provide an opportunity to examine how Buddhist thought and ethical principles can contribute to contemporary discussions on education, sustainability, cultural preservation and peaceful coexistence.
Institutional Coordination and Public Facilitation
The exposition is being undertaken through coordinated efforts of the Ministry of Culture, Government of Arunachal Pradesh, National Museum, International Buddhist Confederation and other concerned institutions.
The National Museum, New Delhi, as the nodal agency, is responsible for the technical and conservation aspects of the Holy Relics, including their secure handling, transportation, installation and safe return.
The Government of Arunachal Pradesh is coordinating arrangements at the respective venues, including security, reception, infrastructure, crowd management, medical facilities, sanitation, local transportation and public facilitation.
The International Buddhist Confederation is facilitating religious coordination, participation of venerable monks, associated cultural and scholarly programmes, the Piprahwa exhibition and the international conference.
The Ministry of Defence and the Indian Air Force have been approached for the requisite aircraft and helicopter support for movement of the Holy Relics, taking into account the challenging terrain and operational requirements of Arunachal Pradesh.
Media coverage and public outreach are being coordinated with the concerned agencies to disseminate information regarding the exposition and associated programmes.
The arrangements are intended to ensure that public veneration is conducted in an orderly, secure and dignified manner, while maintaining the highest standards of religious sanctity and conservation.
A Shared Message of Peace, Compassion and Harmony
The exposition of the Holy Relics of Lord Buddha in Arunachal Pradesh represents an important occasion for spiritual reflection, cultural participation and the celebration of India's Buddhist heritage.
By bringing the Sacred Relics to Tawang, Bomdila and Namsai, the initiative will provide devotees from different Buddhist traditions an opportunity to participate in public veneration and reaffirm their shared spiritual inheritance.
The accompanying exhibition and international conference will further enrich the occasion by connecting religious devotion with historical understanding, scholarship and cultural exchange.
The exposition also carries a message of wider significance. The teachings of Lord Buddha—compassion, non-violence, wisdom, moderation and peaceful coexistence continue to offer valuable guidance to humanity in an increasingly interconnected world.
Through the preservation of sacred heritage and its responsible dissemination, the Government of India seeks to strengthen cultural understanding, encourage people-to-people connections and promote the enduring message of peace and harmony associated with Bhagwan Buddha.
The exposition will conclude on 21 November 2026 with the ceremonial return of the Holy Relics to the National Museum, New Delhi.

title: DRDO leads thematic session on ‘Semiconductors & Next-Generation Chips’ and showcases advanced technologies at ESTIC 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) participated in the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026 held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi from October 27 to 29, 2026. The conclave with the theme ‘Creative Minds, Catalysing Science, Empowering Society’, was inaugurated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and was jointly organised by 12 ministries/departments under the guidance of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India. The event showcased cutting-edge research, deep-tech breakthroughs, and thought provoking discussions with Nobel Laureates, global experts, policymakers, and emerging leaders - igniting a new era of scientific leadership.
DRDO, as one of the key organisers, led the thematic session on ‘Semiconductors & Next-Generation Chips’. Chaired by Distinguished Scientist and Director General, Electronics and Communication Systems (ECS) Dr BK Das, the session brought together eminent leaders from the industry, academia, indigenous chip-development ecosystem and defence electronics.
A panel discussion, moderated by Dr BK Das, was also organised as part of the session, with Distinguished Scientist and Director General (Micro Electronic Devices, Computational Systems & Cyber Systems) Dr Sheena Rani among the panellists. The discussions explored emerging developments in semiconductor technologies, purpose-built Artificial Intelligence (AI) System-on-Chips (SoCs), intelligence at the silicon edge and the evolving microprocessor landscape. The session also highlighted DRDO's evolving role in enabling industries and start-ups to develop game-changing solutions, accelerate next-generation chip design and strengthen indigenous core technologies.
The DRDO Outreach Stall at ESTIC 2026 showcased key initiatives, achievements, research programmes and contributions of the Ministry of Defence towards science, technology and innovation. It featured a diverse range of indigenous technologies developed by DRDO laboratories, including advanced communication systems, quantum technology prototypes, extreme-cold-weather clothing, PRABALA female full-body protector, passive and powered exoskeletons, portable hybrid energy management systems, high-power pulse laser diodes and scramjet engine technology.
DRDO also participated in the Thematic and Departmental Exhibitions at the conclave. At the thematic exhibition on ‘Semiconductors and Next-Generation Chips’, DRDO showcased its achievements in two critical semiconductor technology domains: Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuits (MMICs) and Infrared Focal Plane Arrays (IRFPAs), developed by the Solid State Physics Laboratory (SSPL), Delhi.
Gallium Arsenide (GaAs) and Gallium Nitride (GaN)-based MMICs, along with Multi-Chip Modules (MCMs), displayed at the exhibition have been employed in several strategic missions. These technologies serve as essential building blocks for advanced radar systems and Electronic Warfare (EW) applications. The IRFPAs, on the other hand, serve as the sensing elements or 'eyes' of tactical missiles, enabling target detection and tracking during the terminal phase through Imaging Infrared (IIR) seekers. The exhibits covered a broad range of infrared technologies, including Short-Wave Infrared (SWIR), Mid-Wave Infrared (MWIR) and Long-Wave Infrared (LWIR), demonstrating DRDO's extensive indigenous capabilities in advanced semiconductor technologies.
Other notable DRDO exhibits included scramjet engine technology and neuromorphic accelerators, highlighting breakthroughs in complex and emerging technological domains. The exhibition also featured advanced communication systems, Quantum Random Number Generators (QRNGs), protective equipment, exoskeletons, portable hybrid energy management systems, Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs) and laser proximity sensors.
Semiconductor technology is a critical enabler of national sovereignty, economic strength and digital security. It plays a pivotal role in advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 and Aatmanirbhar Bharat by strengthening indigenous technological capabilities. From communication devices and advanced sensing systems to sophisticated defence platforms, semiconductor chips determine the performance, efficiency and reliability of modern technologies. Beyond chip manufacturing, technological self-reliance requires comprehensive capabilities in chip design, fabrication, testing, industrial-scale production and resilient supply chains.
India aspires to emerge as a globally competitive, dependable and technologically self-reliant semiconductor powerhouse by 2047, with leadership in selected next-generation chip technologies. This vision encompasses the development of a vibrant and sustainable semiconductor ecosystem, generation of high-value employment opportunities and delivery of inclusive societal benefits.
Over the years, India's strategic defence laboratories and specialised semiconductor foundries, including SSPL, Gallium Arsenide Enabling Technology Centre (GAETEC), Semiconductor Technology and Applied Research Centre (STARC) and Semiconductor Laboratory (SCL), have developed specialised competencies in Gallium Arsenide (GaAs), Gallium Nitride (GaN), Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems (MEMS) and mature silicon process technologies.

title: Union Environment Minister visits CAQM’s ‘PAVAN-I3C’ Integrated Command and Control Centre to review Air Pollution Mitigation Operations
subtitle:
PAVAN-I3C integrates 30+ Data Streams for Real-time Monitoring and Data-driven Compliance Management of Air Quality across Delhi-NCR

A Paradigm Shift from Reacting to Air Pollution to Anticipating and Acting on it in Real-time: Shri Bhupender Yadav
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 4:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today visited the Commission for Air Quality Management’s (CAQM) newly developed Integrated Command and Control Centre (I3C), named PAVAN (Platform for Air quality Vigilance and Analytics for NCR), in New Delhi. The Minister reviewed its technological framework and operational readiness. Developed as a single-window digital nerve centre, PAVAN-I3C integrates more than 30 APIs and data streams, including air quality, emissions, meteorological, satellite, camera, mobility, complaint and compliance data from multiple agencies. It also integrates data from 111 Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS) operational in Delhi-NCR, over 2,300 industries, more than 3,200 active construction sites and traffic congestion hotspots.
Addressing the media during the review, Union Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav emphasized that the first priority in tackling regional air pollution is ensuring precise, hyper-local data and absolute transparency. He remarked that the launch of the PAVAN-I3C marks a definitive turning point by eliminating operational lag, dismantling data silos and enabling State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs) to work under a single, verified source of information to hold polluters accountable in minutes. Appreciating the effort, Shri Yadav said, “Clean air cannot be secured by any one agency or any one State acting alone. The I3C brings every data stream that matters onto a single screen, so that a farm fire, a polluting stack or an uncovered construction site is seen, flagged and acted upon in real time. This is a paradigm shift from reacting to pollution to anticipating it, and every implementing agency must now act in real-time on these alerts without delay.” The Minister added that the non-conforming industries, non-compliant polluting sources and traffic congestion hotspots would be swiftly acted upon due to the PAVAN I3C platform. In this background, he further said that construction and demolition (C&D) activities across the NCR region would be halted from 5th to 20th November in a bid to control pollution.
Shri Yadav informed that operating on the principle of
‘Detect, Analyse, Act’
,
the PAVAN-I3C brings together data from multiple agencies on a common platform for real-time and historical analysis of pollution levels, identification of pollution sources, assessment of trends and effectiveness of measures, and tracking of
field-level compliance
against prescribed standards and action plans. It marks a shift towards comprehensive, real-time air quality monitoring and data-driven cross-border enforcement. A defining capability of PAVAN-I3C is its alert-based compliance management. Shri Yadav highlighted that deviations from prescribed norms, Statutory Directions or agreed compliance requirements trigger alerts and escalation to the concerned agency for necessary action. This shifts CAQM from manual, agency-reported monitoring to proactive, digital and
data-driven compliance management
, enabling timely intervention and regulatory action. By integrating air quality data from multiple agencies, the I3C would
strengthen inter-agency coordination
, accelerate enforcement, facilitate
rapid resolution of public grievances
and enable immediate response to localized pollution spikes during critical seasonal periods ensuring a citizen-centric approach, he added.
During the visit, Shri Yadav reviewed key monitoring modules covering
air quality and pollutant concentrations
from CAAQMS installed by CPCB, IMD and SPCBs;
industrial emissions
data on PM, SO₂, NOx and CO from Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS);
satellite-based crop residue burning
data from IARI, ISRO and FIRMS, including comparison with fire events over the previous six years; live camera feeds and PM sensors at
Construction and Demolition
sites;
weather
, rainfall, wind speed and direction and humidity data; live feeds from major
landfill sites
including Okhla, Bhalswa, Ghazipur, Greater Noida and Bhandwari;
vehicular data
through VAHAN and traffic congestion hotspots;
citizen complaints
through the Green Delhi App and SAMEER App; live tracking of Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines
(MRSMs)
; and
compliance by brick kilns
in Haryana and Punjab with prescribed biomass-fuel requirements. The
State Action Plan monitoring module
provides a consolidated view of pending actions at State, sector and action-point levels for Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, covering air quality monitoring, crop residue management, vehicular pollution, C&D activities, road dust management, municipal solid waste management, industrial pollution, DG sets and green crematoria.
Dignitaries present on the occasion included Chairperson (CAQM), Shri Rajesh Verma; Chairperson (CPCB) & Additional Secretary (MoEFCC), Dr. Amandeep Garg, besides other senior officials from the Ministry, CAQM and CPCB.

subtitle:

Padmaja Chunduru (Former MD & CEO, Indian Bank), Shri N S Vishwanathan (Former Deputy Governor, RBI) as the Members

The ‘High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat’ was announced in the Budget 2026-27 by Union Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman


 Committee to review India’s Banking Sector and recommend reforms to make it aligned with the goals of Viksit Bharat, 2047
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 7:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Government of India has constituted a High Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat to undertake a review of India’s banking sector and recommend structural, institutional, regulatory and legislative reforms necessary to make it globally competitive, financially inclusive, and resilient for Viksit Bharat, 2047. Union Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman during her Budget speech 2026-27 had announced setting up of the Committee.
Shri Suresh N. Patel, former Central Vigilance Commissioner will be the Chairman of the Committee. Besides, three distinguished experts- Shri Shirish Chandra Murmu (Deputy Governor, Reserve Bank of India), Smt. Padmaja Chunduru (Former MD & CEO, Indian Bank) and Shri N S Vishwanathan (Former Deputy Governor, Reserve Bank of India) will be the members of the Committee. The Joint Secretary (Banking), Department of Financial Services will be the Member Secretary of the Committee. The tenure of the Committee shall be six months.
The Terms of Reference of the Committee are as follows:
Assess the present banking practices and prudential norms, identifying global best practices, and adapt them suitably for the Indian banking system, while also providing a roadmap for creating globally competitive banks.
Review the existing regulatory and legal frameworks for banks, including Regional Rural Banks and Cooperative Banks, and suggest reforms to bring in efficiency and enable ease of doing banking for Viksit Bharat.
Undertake assessment of the long-term capital requirements for banks, including Development Financial Institutions and Non-Banking Financial Companies, with recommendations on funding sources and enabling mechanisms to support credit growth.
Examine differences in cost of capital for business, and suggest policy options to boost private investment for sustainable growth.
Prepare a roadmap for AI and digital innovation in banking institutions, while providing for safeguards against cyber risks. Further, to suggest a strategy for talent acquisition and capacity building to ensure a future-ready workforce for the banking sector.
Review the Priority Sector Lending framework and Lead Bank Scheme to assess their relevance, effectiveness, and coordination in promoting inclusive, balanced, and data-driven credit delivery aligned with evolving economic priorities and financial inclusion goals.
Make recommendations on any other matter referred to the Committee by the Government of India.

title: DRI deals major blow to Myanmar-linked drug smuggling network; seizes huge consignment of 50 kg methamphetamine tablets and crystal meth in North-East; four arrested
subtitle: In another a major intelligence-led operation, DRI uncovers innovative concealment methods involving furniture and tea packets; three vehicles seized
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In another significant crackdown on cross-border narcotics smuggling in North East, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), has seized large quantity of
50 kg methamphetamine in the form of tablets (Yaba) and crystal meth
, in two back-to-back Intelligence led operations in Mizoram and Assam. The seizures comprise of significantly large quantities of 30 kg methamphetamine tablets and 20 kg crystal methamphetamine. Four persons have been arrested under the relevant provisions of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985.
Acting on specific intelligence inputs regarding the transportation of multiple consignments of narcotic drugs from Zokhawthar towards Aizawl and Silchar, the officers of DRI, with operational assistance from the Assam Rifles intercepted a Mahindra Bolero Camper   on the outskirts of Aizawl along the Aizawl–Champhai Road, on 29th October 2026. A thorough search of the vehicle led to the recovery of
30 brick-sized packets containing pinkish-orange tablets, weighing 30 kg
, concealed in a specially constructed cavity inside an office table with a storage cabinet. The use of furniture as cover cargo to camouflage the transportation of narcotics represents a novel modus operandi, apparently intended to make the vehicle appear to be transporting ordinary household or office goods.
On 30th Oct 2026, in another intelligence led operation
, the officers of DRI, assisted by the Assam Rifles, intercepted an Ashok Leyland truck and a Bolero Camper at Dholai, approximately 40 km from Silchar. A search of the truck resulted in the recovery
of 20 packets crystal methamphetamine, weighing 20 kg.
The packets had been concealed above the driver's cabin and packed in tea packets bearing foreign markings, apparently to evade detection. Field testing indicated the presence of amphetamine in the recovered substance.
In two operations, four persons have been arrested under the NDPS Act, 1985. In addition, all three vehicles used for transporting the contraband have been seized.
Preliminary investigation indicates that the seized drugs were smuggled from Myanmar. The seizure comes in the backdrop of DRI's recent two major seizures of 232 kg and 56 kg of methamphetamine in the North-Eastern region. Together, these successive seizures underscore the scale and persistence of cross-border synthetic drug trafficking as well as DRI's sustained efforts to identify and dismantle the networks facilitating the movement of such drugs from across the international border into the country.
DRI remains committed to disrupting organised narcotics trafficking networks, preventing the proliferation of synthetic drugs and safeguarding the country from the serious social and public health consequences of drug abuse.

title: Fisheries Sector Looks Beyond Production: Fish Value Addition Enterprises and Mobile Marketing Set to Transform High-Value India’s Blue Economy
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 7:55AM by PIB Delhi
content:
India’s fisheries sector is evolving from a production-focused activity into a dynamic, technology-driven and value-oriented pillar of the national economy. It plays a vital role in strengthening food and nutritional security, generating employment, supporting rural livelihoods and contributing to export earnings.
The fisheries ecosystem has witnessed significant transformation through value addition, cold-chain development, modern processing, mobile fish marketing and start-up-led innovation. Enterprises are increasingly adopting Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things, blockchain, drone technology, smart cold-chain systems and precision aquaculture to improve traceability, productivity, quality assurance and post-harvest management. Together, these interventions are reducing losses, enhancing profitability and strengthening the fisheries value chain.
Value addition is emerging as a critical lever in reshaping India’s fisheries sector from a primary production activity into a diversified and market-oriented enterprise. By enabling fish and fishery products to be processed, packaged, branded and made available in ready-to-cook or ready-to-eat formats, it allows producers to secure better prices while responding to changing consumer preferences in domestic and export markets. More importantly, value addition helps reduce post-harvest losses, extend shelf life and improve quality standards across the supply chain. It also opens new avenues of employment and entrepreneurship, particularly for fishers, fish farmers, women’s groups, youth, cooperatives and small enterprises engaged in processing, packaging, cold-chain logistics, marketing and retail. In doing so, value addition strengthens market linkages, enhances incomes and positions the fisheries sector to compete more effectively in the growing market for safe, convenient and high-quality seafood.
This shift towards value-addition has been supported by a series of public investments and targeted policy interventions aimed at strengthening the sector from production to markets. Since 2015, the Government of India has significantly stepped-up public investment in the fisheries sector, committing Rs. 39,272 crore through key schemes and programmes such as the Blue Revolution Scheme, Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), Pradhan Mantri Matsya Samridhi Sah Yojana (PM-MKSSY) and Kisan Credit Card (KCC). These interventions are aimed at expanding infrastructure, strengthening production and post-harvest systems, and creating employment and livelihood opportunities for 74.66 lakh fishers and fish farmers across the country.
A parallel focus has been placed on strengthening transportation and logistics networks, with
46,500 facilities
,
including fish transportation systems, retail and wholesale
fish
markets, kiosks, feed mills, ice plants, cold storages and value-added enterprise units,
added
with an investment of Rs
. 3,393
.85 crore
. In addition, five modern and smart fish markets are under development, integrating advanced IT systems, green technologies and logistics supply chains, and are expected to generate 15,900 employment opportunities.
Alongside infrastructure and logistics, the availability of quality raw material is equally critical for sustaining premium fish value chains. As India looks to expand value addition around premium fish products, ensuring a steady supply of quality raw material has become increasingly important. In this direction, the Department has taken up genetic improvement initiatives to develop fish varieties with faster growth, improved disease resistance, better resilience and higher productivity. The effort is expected to support the availability of high-value species such as
trout, shrimp, catla, rohu, tilapia, pangasius, seabass and scampi
for domestic consumption, processing and export-oriented markets. By strengthening the production base for such species, genetic improvement can complement value-added enterprises, improve farm-level returns and help India move up the fisheries value chain.
For these gains to reach small producers, institutional models that can aggregate production and improve access to markets are becoming increasingly important. The push towards value addition in fisheries is also being anchored in collective enterprise models that can help small fishers and fish farmers overcome constraints of scale, capital and market access. The Department has supported the formation of 2,195 Fisheries Farmer Producer Organizations (FFPOs) enabling producers to aggregate output, pool resources and participate more effectively in processing, branding and marketing activities. Several of these organisations have also been integrated with the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), widening their access to digital markets and improving prospects for fair price realisation. Under PM-MKSSY, 5,500 fisheries cooperatives are being strengthened to function as FFPOs in collaboration with intermediary agencies such as NCDC, NAFED, SFAC and NERAMAC. By building collective bargaining power and linking producer groups with modern value chains, these institutions are expected to support a more inclusive transition towards value-added fisheries enterprises.
The emphasis on value addition is also creating a stronger platform for women’s participation in post-harvest activities and fisheries-based enterprises. Women have emerged as a vital force in India’s fisheries sector, particularly in post-harvest operations and small-scale enterprises, where value addition has opened new avenues for income generation and entrepreneurship. Their empowerment has been prioritised under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), under which projects worth more than Rs. 4,155 crore, with a central share of Rs. 1,572 crore have been approved over the last five years for the benefit of more than 1.28 lakh women beneficiaries. This support has enabled women to participate in diverse such as fish drying, preparation of fish pickles and papad, smoked fish products, fish powder, and packaging and retailing. Mobile fish vending units and micro‑processing enterprises are generating sustainable livelihoods for women across coastal, inland, and northeastern states, while also strengthening nutritional security by expanding access to affordable, protein‑rich food.
India’s fisheries sector is increasingly moving beyond production towards a value-chain-driven and technology-enabled ecosystem, supported by investments in processing, logistics, cold-chain infrastructure, digital platforms and entrepreneurship. With the convergence of PMMSY, PM-MKSSY, FIDF and KCC, the sector is better positioned to reduce post-harvest losses, expand value-added seafood exports, improve fisher incomes, promote women-led enterprises and generate rural employment. The future of Indian fisheries will depend not merely on producing more fish, but on building resilient, market-oriented value chains that connect fishers and fish farmers with consumers through innovation, mobility, processing and sustainable market development.

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 7:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Posts today issued commemorative postage stamps on breast cancer awareness to mark International Breast Cancer Awareness Month. The initiative, conceptualised and undertaken by the Department of Posts, seeks to leverage the extensive postal network to disseminate messages on breast cancer awareness, early detection and preventive healthcare. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare provided technical inputs, reference materials and background information to support the development of the health-related content of the commemorative stamps and postcards.
During the Event, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Health Secretary, along with DG Postal Services, Smt. Manisha Sinha released the two commemorative postage stamps and a set of picture postcards dedicated to breast cancer awareness.
Speaking on the occasion, Smt. Srivastava emphasised the foundational role of women's health in building healthy families and, therefore, a healthy nation. Underscoring the importance of prioritising women's health and preventive care, she highlighted the Swasth Nari, Sashakt Parivar Abhiyaan, conducted from September 17 to October 2 last year, which placed a special focus on women's health through screening and awareness initiatives.
Further in her address, she reiterated the Government’s commitment to addressing the growing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in the country. In this regard, Smt. Srivastava highlighted the Ministry’s efforts under the
National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD)
, which integrates screening for oral, breast and cervical cancers into primary healthcare services across more than 1.8 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs. She also underscored the role of the NP-NCD portal and ABHA IDs under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission in ensuring accessible health records and continuity of care across healthcare facilities.
Under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD), a total of 86.97 crore screenings have been conducted for oral, breast and cervical cancers across the country. This includes 49.02 crore screenings for oral cancer, 22.90 crore for breast cancer and 14.05 crore for cervical cancer. Of these, 5.50 lakh individuals are currently undergoing treatment, including 2.70 lakh oral cancer patients, 1.43 lakh breast cancer patients and 1.37 lakh cervical cancer patients. She appreciated the Department of Posts for organising the commemorative event during the same period this year, noting that it would help carry forward the campaign's message and strengthen public awareness about breast cancer.
The Union Health Secretary noted that India reported more than two lakh new breast cancer cases in 2024, with an estimated one in every 29 women at risk of developing the disease. She underscored the critical role of early detection in improving treatment outcomes, and highlighted that delayed diagnosis remains a concern despite growing awareness and the availability of screening facilities. She urged women to prioritise preventive healthcare through regular screening and self-examination, and encouraged the public to make greater use of available government healthcare services and digital health platforms to facilitate timely detection and treatment.
Director General Postal Services, Smt. Manisha Sinha, highlighted the significance of the postal network in carrying important public messages to the last mile. She noted that commemorative stamps serve as enduring instruments of public awareness and reflect the country's priorities. She emphasised that the extensive reach of postal services would help take the message of breast cancer awareness to communities across the country, encouraging timely screening and fostering support for women affected by the disease. She also acknowledged the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare for providing technical inputs, reference materials and background information for the initiative, which helped in developing the health-related content of the commemorative stamps and postcards.
The programme concluded with an address by Additional Director General Dr. Pushp Lata, who highlighted that breast cancer is the most common cancer among women in India, accounting for more than 30% of all new cancer cases diagnosed among women. Emphasising the importance of early detection, she noted that timely diagnosis significantly improves treatment outcomes and quality of life, adding that nearly one-third of breast cancer cases are preventable and another one-third can be cured if detected early. She outlined the continuum of cancer care, from screening and referral at the primary healthcare level to diagnostic confirmation and treatment at district hospitals, State Cancer Institutes and Tertiary Cancer Care Centres. She also highlighted the establishment of Daycare Cancer Centres to improve access to chemotherapy closer to patients' homes. She called for regular screening, timely treatment and a need to address fear, stigma and barriers to healthcare access to improve health outcomes for women.
The day’s events brought together the collaborative efforts of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Department of Posts in taking the message of breast cancer awareness to the public. The release of the commemorative stamps aims to strengthen awareness about breast cancer, lays particular emphasis on self-examination and early detection, and encourages regular screening. The initiative underscores the significance of timely diagnosis and preventive healthcare in improving outcomes for women combating the disease.
About Breast Cancer Awareness Month
Observed annually from October 1 to 31, Breast Cancer Awareness Month is an international health campaign aimed at promoting early detection, education, and garnering support for those affected by the disease.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Yogi Adityanath and Union Minister for Railways Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw will flag off new Vande Bharat Sleeper Express services between Varanasi and New Delhi from Varanasi tomorrow.
Following the introduction of Vande Bharat Sleeper services on the Howrah-Guwahati corridor and the corresponding return journey in January 2026, the new services will extend the benefits of this next-generation train to additional regions. With enhanced onboard amenities, advanced safety features and thoughtfully designed sleeper accommodation, Indian Railways is working towards making long-distance overnight journeys more comfortable, reliable and passenger-centric.
Varanasi-New Delhi: Enhancing Connectivity Between a Major Pilgrimage Centre and the National Capital
The Vande Bharat Sleeper service between Varanasi and New Delhi will strengthen connectivity between one of India's most prominent spiritual and cultural destinations and the national capital.
Varanasi attracts pilgrims, domestic and international tourists, students and other visitors throughout the year. Improved overnight connectivity with New Delhi will provide greater convenience to passengers travelling for religious, educational, professional, administrative and tourism-related purposes.
The service will connect Varanasi, Prayagraj, Kanpur Central, Aligarh and Ghaziabad, before reaching New Delhi. These stations serve important urban centres and provide connectivity to surrounding districts, helping extend the benefits of modern rail travel to a wider passenger base.
The new service will depart Varanasi at 20:50 and arrive in New Delhi at 06:10 the following morning. In the return direction, it will depart New Delhi at 21:40 and reach Varanasi at 07:10 the following day.
Compared with the existing Shiv Ganga Express, the Vande Bharat Sleeper Express will reduce journey time from Varanasi to New Delhi by 55 minutes and from New Delhi to Varanasi by 35 minutes, offering passengers a faster overnight travel option in both directions.
The service will operate six days a week, except on Fridays for the Varanasi-originating service and on Saturdays for the New Delhi-originating service. The overnight schedule will allow passengers to travel during the evening and reach their destination the following morning, helping them make more effective use of their time. The service is expected to be particularly beneficial for pilgrims, tourists, students, working professionals and families who frequently travel between eastern Uttar Pradesh and the national capital region.
Vande Bharat Sleeper: A New Standard in Overnight Passenger Travel
Designed specifically for long-distance journeys, the Vande Bharat Sleeper combines modern technology, improved safety systems and passenger-friendly amenities to enhance the overnight travel experience. Its design focuses on providing a comfortable environment for passengers travelling over extended distances, with particular attention to sleeping arrangements, cleanliness, safety, accessibility and convenience.

title: Geospatial capabilities will be a key determinant of India’s future economic growth: Dr. Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
Dr. Jitendra Singh calls for stronger Government-industry partnership to advance India’s geospatial economy

“Enable, invest and adopt” is the way forward for the geospatial sector: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Dr. Jitendra Singh urges departments to work with Survey of India on geospatial applications

Dr. Jitendra Singh calls for a business-friendly environment to unlock the geospatial sector’s potential in roundtable discussion
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 OCT 2026 5:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Delivering the keynote address at a workshop on “Government & Industry Synergy for Geospatial Transformation: Co-Creating the Geospatial Economy for Viksit Bharat 2047” in New Delhi today, Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, the Department of Atomic Energy and the Department of Space, said geospatial capabilities would be a key determinant of India’s future economic growth. The workshop was organised by the Survey of India under the Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India.
The Minister also participated in a roundtable discussion with senior Government officials and industry leaders on opportunities, challenges and perspectives for taking the geospatial sector forward.
Dr. Jitendra Singh inaugurated the exhibition and interacted with exhibitors. He said geospatial information had evolved from a technical resource for mapping and surveying into a strategic national asset for economic growth. Several far-reaching geospatial reforms had been undertaken over the past 12–13 years with the encouragement of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he said, adding that implementing them had required courage and conviction.
The Minister highlighted the transformation of the Survey of India from an organisation focused on traditional, labour-intensive surveying to one adapting to satellite-based mapping, drones and computer-based technologies. Recalling his visit to its Dehradun campus, he said its historic working arrangements reflected the physical demands of surveying in earlier times, while today’s work required young professionals with technology and computing skills.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also called for stronger public-private partnerships to expand markets, develop viable business models and encourage startups and MSMEs. He said the National Geospatial Policy 2022 provided an open framework that could accommodate emerging technologies, including geospatial artificial intelligence (AI). Describing AI as a tool that could improve the speed and precision of work, he said its use should be encouraged across sectors.
The Minister urged Government departments to identify areas in which they could work with the Survey of India and asked the Surveyor General to organise virtual meetings to familiarise them with the organisation’s capabilities. Wider awareness, he said, could help departments and private industry identify opportunities for collaboration. Emphasising industry’s role in advancing the sector, he said the way forward was to “enable, invest and adopt”—enabling to build confidence, investing to develop capability, and adopting geospatial solutions to generate economic growth
Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science & Technology, said geospatial infrastructure could help organise information on national resources and support their optimal use, including during the energy transition. He noted that the National Geospatial Policy 2022 recognised DST as the nodal agency for the geospatial domain and provided for a liberal environment for the generation, accessibility and use of data.
Prof. Waghmare highlighted the convergence of satellite and drone technologies, artificial intelligence, optics and rapid data processing. He said Government priorities should be informed by real-world applications and industry requirements. Geospatial infrastructure could support India’s diverse needs, promote indigenous innovation and entrepreneurship, strengthen global partnerships and help address challenges such as climate change, he added.
Shri S. K. Sinha, Surveyor General of India, thanked Dr. Jitendra Singh for his guidance and support in advancing geospatial reforms. He said the National Geospatial Policy 2022 had laid the foundation for an open, innovation-driven ecosystem, and that Government, industry and academia would need to work together to translate geospatial potential into economic opportunity. The Survey of India was working with industry to support flagship Government programmes through foundational geospatial data and positioning infrastructure, he said, expressing confidence that the workshop would help turn the shared vision into collaborative action.
During the roundtable discussion, the Minister said that the Government is committed to creating a more business-friendly and facilitative environment by simplifying procedures, removing unnecessary regulations and encouraging innovation. Emphasising the importance of collaboration between the government and private sector, the Minister highlighted successful models in sectors such as space and biotechnology that can be replicated to accelerate growth. He also encouraged stakeholders to identify procedural bottlenecks, leverage government support mechanisms and work together to unlock the immense potential of the geospatial sector.
The workshop was attended by Shri S. K. Sinha, Surveyor General of India; Shri Srikant Sastri, Chairman, Geospatial Data Promotion & Development Committee (GDPDC); and Prof. Umesh V. Waghmare, Secretary, Department of Science & Technology (DST).

content:
The
National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT),under the Ministry of Textiles
, Government of India, has made significant achievements under Special Campaign 6 by undertaking a comprehensive range of cleanliness, sanitation, waste management, infrastructure maintenance and environmental sustainability initiatives across its campus. NIFT Delhi campus on 2 October 2026
in the august presence of
Secretary, Ministry of Textiles and other senior officers and Directors
. The participation of the senior leadership marked the commencement of the campaign and reinforced the Ministry's commitment towards promoting cleanliness, environmental protection and sustainable institutional practices.
Conducted from 2 October to 31 October 2026
, the campaign aimed to create a cleaner, greener, safer and more sustainable campus environment through active participation of students, faculty and staff.
Comprehensive Cleanliness and Improved Campus Hygiene
Extensive cleanliness activities were undertaken across academic blocks, workshops, canteens, hostels, corridors, rooftops, storage areas and other common spaces. Removal of cobwebs, accumulated dust, garbage and unwanted materials, along with cleaning of furniture, fans, computer equipment, water tanks and drainage systems, contributed to improved campus hygiene and sanitation.
Effective Waste Management and Digital Housekeeping
Special emphasis was placed on waste segregation and responsible disposal. E-waste and scrap were taken up for disposal in accordance with prescribed procedures. Disposal of e-files and weeding out of physical records were also undertaken to strengthen digital housekeeping, improve record management and optimise available storage space.
Environmental Sustainability and Green Practices
As part of its environmental initiatives, NIFT undertook plantation, horticulture, tree trimming and pruning activities to enhance campus greenery. A demonstration on preparing biodegradable compost using leaves, fruit waste and leftover food items was also organized to promote the productive utilization of organic waste and encourage environmentally responsible practices.
‘Craft from Waste’ – Promoting Creativity and Reuse
In an innovative initiative reflecting NIFT's creative and design-oriented ethos, the institute undertook the ‘Craft from Waste’ activity, demonstrating how discarded materials can be transformed into useful and decorative articles. These creatively prepared items were also used to beautify identified campus areas, promoting the principles of reuse, recycling and waste reduction.
Infrastructure Maintenance and Campus Beautification
Several maintenance activities were undertaken to improve campus infrastructure, safety and functionality. These included inspection and rectification of electrical installations, repair of defective switches, sockets and hanging wires, maintenance of lifts, hostel buildings, doors,
furniture, fixtures and perimeter fencing. Anti-termite treatment and pest control activities were also carried out across academic, administrative and residential blocks.Further, cleaning and maintenance of heaters, blowers, geysers, HVAC systems, air conditioners, Air Handling Units (AHUs) and air filtration units were undertaken to ensure a clean, hygienic and safe campus environment.
Student Participation and Awareness Activities
To encourage awareness and active participation, NIFT organised various competitions and awareness activities during the campaign. These included a slogan-making competition on the theme ‘Importance of Swachhata and E-Waste Management’, along with painting and poem competitions on Swachhata. Posters, banners, placards and standees were also displayed at prominent locations to spread awareness about cleanliness and environmental protection. Winners of the competitions were felicitated to encourage their continued participation.
Recognition of Housekeeping and Hygiene Personnel
Recognising the valuable contribution of sanitation and housekeeping personnel, NIFT felicitated its housekeeping and hygiene workers on 27 October 2026 for their dedicated efforts in maintaining cleanliness and sanitation across the campus. The initiative acknowledged their important role in maintaining a clean and healthy institutional environment and reinforced the principle of dignity of labour.
Through its dedicated efforts under Special Campaign 6,
NIFT has reaffirmed its commitment to the vision of the Ministry of Texti
les for promoting cleanliness, environmental sustainability and responsible resource management. The campaign has demonstrated that collective participation, innovative practices and sustained efforts can bring meaningful improvements in institutional cleanliness and environmental protection. These initiatives will further encourage a culture of cleanliness, creativity and sustainability, contributing towards the vision of a cleaner, greener and more sustainable India.

date:

content:
The 14th International Tourism Mart (ITM), organised by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, in association with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh and other North Eastern States, successfully concluded its main sessions today in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh. The Mart is being organised from 29 to 31 October 2026, which brought together domestic and international tourism stakeholders to showcase the tourism potential of the North Eastern Region, strengthen business partnerships and promote sustainable and experience-based tourism.
The Mart witnessed participation of 43 international buyers from 22 countries, 42 domestic buyers from 16 States and Union Territories and 81 sellers, along with media representatives, influencers and tourism stakeholders. The participating countries included Australia, Belarus, Bhutan, Egypt, France, Germany, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Kenya, Malaysia, the Philippines, Poland, Russia, Singapore, South Korea, Spain, Sri Lanka, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom and the United States.
The Mart
’
s deliberations concluded with the Regional Meeting of Tourism Ministers of the North Eastern States, held on 30 October 2026 under the chairmanship of Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat. The meeting brought together Tourism Ministers and senior officials from the North Eastern States to discuss tourism development priorities, regional cooperation, emerging tourism opportunities and measures to improve tourist facilitation across the region.
During the meeting, thematic presentations were made to the Tourism Ministers on Dekho Apna Desh 2.0 and the National Digital Tourism Stack (NDTS). The presentation on Dekho Apna Desh 2.0 focused on the Mission for Redistribution of Tourism Demand and Promotion of Lesser-Known Destinations, aimed at promoting tourism-ready destinations as alternatives to popular tourist centres. The presentation on NDTS highlighted the development of a common digital tourism ecosystem to improve the discoverability of tourism experiences, enable online bookings and enhance market access for local tourism service providers, including guides, homestays and tourism entrepreneurs.
Presentations were also made on the Live Concert Economy and Restricted Area Permit (RAP)/Protected Area Permit (PAP) requirements in the North Eastern Region. The discussions on the live events economy highlighted the potential of music concerts, cultural festivals and other events to attract tourists, encourage longer stays and generate opportunities for local businesses. The presentation on RAP/PAP requirements focused on improving tourist facilitation through simplified application procedures, greater clarity on permit requirements and timely processing, while taking into account security considerations. Tourism Ministers from the eight North Eastern States also shared their views and suggestions on tourism development priorities and regional cooperation.
A major component of the International Tourism Mart was the structured business-to-business (B2B) meetings, which provided a platform for direct engagement between domestic and international buyers and tourism sellers. A total number of 1580 B2B meetings were held, facilitating opportunities for developing new tourism itineraries, establishing commercial partnerships and promoting tourism products and experiences across the North Eastern States.
Earlier, during the technical sessions, Shri Suman Billa, Additional Secretary and Director General, Ministry of Tourism, delivered the keynote address highlighting India
’
s significant growth in domestic tourism, with Domestic Tourist Visits increasing from 1.32 billion in 2014 to 4.34 billion in 2025, registering a CAGR of approximately 11%. He noted that the tourism sector supports 89 million jobs and contributes 5.22% to the national GDP. Highlighting improvements in connectivity, he stated that the number of airports in the North Eastern
Region has increased from 9 in 2014 to 17, while the national highway network has expanded from 10,905 km to 16,207 km. He also underscored the region
’
s investment potential and opportunities for community-led tourism growth, particularly through homestays, adventure, eco, wellness and experiential tourism.
The technical sessions also featured presentations by all eight North Eastern States—Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura—showcasing their tourism attractions, emerging destinations and tourism circuits.
The Mart was inaugurated on 29 October 2026 in the presence of Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister for Tourism and Culture; Shri Suresh Gopi, Union Minister of State for Tourism and Petroleum & Natural Gas; Shri Pema Khandu, Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh; Shri Prem Singh Tamang, Chief Minister of Sikkim; and other dignitaries. Addressing the inaugural session, Shri Shekhawat emphasised the importance of translating the region
’
s tourism potential into sustainable business opportunities and livelihoods for local communities.
The Mart also showcased the rich cultural and natural heritage of the North Eastern Region through the North East Bazaar, featuring traditional handicrafts, handlooms, textiles and regional products, along with cultural programmes highlighting the traditions of the region. Curated visits for delegates and media representatives included Tawang Monastery, Tawang War Memorial and Urgelling Gompa.
On the last day, technical visits to Buddha Park, PTSO Lake and Shernup Village are scheduled for 31 October 2026. Post-Mart familiarisation (FAM) tours for international delegates will commence from Guwahati on 1 November 2026, providing opportunities to experience tourism destinations and products across the North Eastern Region.
The 14th edition marked the return of the International Tourism Mart to Tawang after 13 years, following the second edition held here in 2013. The Mart reaffirmed the commitment to strengthening tourism partnerships, promoting lesser-known destinations and positioning the North Eastern Region as a leading destination for sustainable and experience-based tourism.

In Vaishali, Bihar, participants took the Loktantrik Shapath, reaffirming their commitment to responsible citizenship. In Rajasthan, programmes in Bundi and Dausa focused on voter awareness and promoting a drug-free lifestyle, with a street play on the importance of voting organised in Dausa. In Uttar Pradesh, Lakhimpur Kheri hosted a Nasha Mukt awareness session and a lecture on Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD), while activities in Shrawasti included youth mobilisation for a drug-free India and a Neighbourhood Youth Parliament.
In Madurai, Tamil Nadu, the Yuva Samvad featured a Parliament-style discussion on the Women’s Reservation Bill, providing young participants an opportunity to deliberate on women's representation and inclusive governance.
With 96 programmes conducted across 27 States and Union Territories so far, the campaign continues to engage young people through discussions, interactions with public representatives and Youth Icons, and activities promoting democratic awareness, responsible citizenship and youth leadership.
